CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES
"Any active suicidal thoughts require immediate emergency medical care," Mitchell advised.
"If a patient develops emergent depression or suicidal ideation during treatment, clinicians should discontinue the weight-loss medication and connect the patient with psychiatric support."
Eli Lilly, manufacturer of the tirzepatide weight-loss medication Zepbound, explicitly mentions "depression or thoughts of suicide" in its safety information.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER
"You should pay attention to changes in your mood, behaviors, feelings or thoughts," the website reads.
It further advises patients to contact a healthcare provider if mental health changes are "new, worse or worry you."
An expert recommends that a physician conducts a baseline mental health history before prescribing new weight-loss medications. (iStock)
On Lilly's medical-information site, the company says that after reviewing clinical trials and medical reports, "no increased risk" of suicidal ideation or psychiatric adverse effects was identified.

Novo Nordisk, manufacturer of the semaglutide weight-loss medication Wegovy, states in its trials that less than 1% of participants experienced suicidal ideation or behavior during treatment. It also says there was "no difference between semaglutide 2.4 mg and placebo."

Fox News Digital reached out to Lilly and Novo Nordisk for comment.

title: Joe Biden shares health update after prostate cancer diagnosis while issuing warning to others
summary: Joe Biden revealed his radiation treatment from last fall "worked as intended" as he urged men to discuss prostate cancer screening with their doctors.
story: Jill Biden admits former President Joe Biden experienced a decline in mental acuity, "slowing down" and "stuttering more" during his term due to exhaustion, despite her urging him to seek re-election. Rep. Claudia Tenney comments on the situation, suggesting it's an opportunity for Jill Biden to gain power, highlighting the former First Lady's own upcoming book.

Former President Joe Biden shared an update on his battle with prostate cancer Tuesday, revealing that radiation treatment he underwent last fall "worked as intended" while urging American men not to delay conversations with their doctors about cancer screening.
Biden, 83, issued the update in a lengthy social media post marking Prostate Cancer Awareness Month, saying the occasion was more personal for him following his diagnosis last year.
"The radiation treatment from last fall worked as intended, and I continue to do the things I care about, like finishing my memoir," Biden wrote.
JILL BIDEN SAYS FORMER PRESIDENT WILL LIVE WITH STAGE 4 CANCER 'FOR THE REST OF HIS LIFE,' HAS SLOWED DOWN
President Joe Biden speaks at the White House in Washington, D.C. (Reuters)
He also thanked the doctors, nurses and other medical professionals who have treated him, saying their "skill, dedication, and compassion mean so much."
Biden used much of the message to urge men to discuss prostate cancer screening with their doctors, pointing to the dramatically higher survival rate when the disease is detected early.
CANCER TREATMENT DELAYS SURGE ACROSS US AS DOCTOR WARNS SYSTEM ‘NEEDS FIXING IMMEDIATELY’

Joe Biden continues radiation therapy for Stage 4 prostate cancer that has metastasized to bone, with aides saying the 83-year-old former president remains active and engaged. (Kyle Mazza/Anadolu via Getty Images)
"Talk to your doctors. Ask the hard questions. Do it for yourself, and do it for the people who love you," Biden wrote.

Biden said men at average risk should begin discussing prostate cancer screening with their doctors around age 50, while Black men and those with a family history should begin those conversations earlier.
SIMPLE SITTING CHANGE LINKED TO LOWER RISK OF CANCER DEATH, STUDY FINDS

The American Cancer Society recommends discussing screening at age 50 for average-risk men, age 45 for Black men and certain men with a family history, and age 40 for some men at even higher risk. (iStock)
The American Cancer Society recommends discussing screening at age 50 for average-risk men, age 45 for Black men and certain men with a family history, and age 40 for some men at even higher risk.
Biden’s office announced in May 2025 that the former president had been diagnosed with an aggressive form of prostate cancer that had metastasized to his bones.
JOE BIDEN'S CANCER HAS SPREAD FURTHER, LEAVING HIM IN 'VERY PAINFUL' CONDITION, HUNTER REVEALS
Former President Joe Biden shared this picture of him and Jill Biden after it was announced he was diagnosed with prostate cancer. (X/JoeBiden)

The diagnosis came after Biden experienced increasing urinary symptoms and doctors discovered a prostate nodule. His office said at the time that the cancer had a Gleason score of 9, Grade Group 5, but was hormone-sensitive, allowing for effective management.
Biden later underwent radiation therapy and completed that course of treatment last fall.
CANCER SURVIVORS SAW MAJOR IMPROVEMENTS IN SLEEP AND WELL-BEING WITH ONE WEEKLY PRACTICE
Biden closed Tuesday's message by thanking those who have continued to pray for him and his family. (Grant Baldwin/Getty Images)
Fox News Digital reached out to Biden’s office for additional comment on his current health, treatment and prognosis.
Biden closed Tuesday's message by thanking those who have continued to pray for him and his family.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"It’s my hope and prayer that by sharing our experience and being part of this important conversation, we can help save lives," he wrote. "And no matter what, keep the faith. God bless you."Fox News Digital's Stepheny Price and Robert McGreevy contributed to this reporting.
Jasmine Baehr is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital, where she covers politics, the military, legal debates surrounding life and family policy, as well as faith and culture.

title: Drug developed for lung disease may slow biological aging in surprising ‘bonus’
summary: Rentosertib, an AI-discovered drug for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, made patients appear three to four years biologically younger in a clinical trial.
story: A drug being developed to treat a serious lung disease may also help to slow the aging process, first author Alex Zhavoronkov, PhD, founder and co-CEO of Insilico Medicine, told Fox News Digital.
A drug being developed to treat a serious lung disease may also help to slow the aging process, researchers say.
In a small clinical study, patients who took rentosertib – developed by Insilico Medicine in Massachusetts – showed changes in blood proteins that made them appear biologically younger.
Several tests estimated that after treatment, the patients were biologically about three to four years younger.
EATING COMMON DAIRY FOOD EVERY DAY MAY SLOW BIOLOGICAL AGING, STUDY SUGGESTS

"There is a promising trend in age reversal in addition to treating the disease, and it came as a bonus for disease treatment," first author Alex Zhavoronkov, PhD, founder and co-CEO of Insilico Medicine, told Fox News Digital.
A drug being developed to treat a serious lung disease may also help to slow the aging process, researchers say. (iStock)
"It basically means that you are predicted to be younger using a validated set of aging clocks. We don’t know what that means yet."
The results were published in Nature Biotechnology and presented Monday at the Nature conference at Sorbonne University in Paris.
ALZHEIMER'S BLOOD TESTS MAY PREDICT SYMPTOMS YEARS IN ADVANCE, BUT EXPERTS URGE CAUTION
The researchers caution, however, that this does not yet prove the drug can actually reverse aging or help people live longer.
"It’s early days," Zhavoronkov noted. "The drug is still investigational."
What is rentosertib?

Rentosertib is an experimental drug, discovered with the help of artificial intelligence, that is being developed to treat idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), a serious disease that causes scarring in the lungs.
In an unexpected outcome, the drug was found to change patterns of proteins in the blood in ways that made patients appear an average of three to four years younger, in one case up to six years.

Rentosertib is an experimental drug, discovered with the help of artificial intelligence, that is being developed to treat idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, a serious disease that causes scarring in the lungs. (iStock)
Six different aging tests showed the same general pattern, with patients who took rentosertib "scoring" biologically younger than those who received a placebo.
The strongest effect was seen after four weeks in patients taking 30 mg of the drug twice a day.
LONGEVITY DOCTOR REVEALS WHAT MATTERS MOST FOR AGING WELL, BEYOND PRICEY BIOHACKS

When researchers compared the results with data from more than 55,000 people in the UK Biobank, they found that the drug changed several blood proteins in the opposite direction from what is normally seen with aging.
The researchers also found signs that the drug may affect aging at the cellular level, as it changed processes involved in how cells function and respond to damage.
"Everybody agrees that living longer should be a fundamental human right for everyone."
Zhavoronkov said the company's approach uses AI to search for what he calls "molecular criminals" — biological targets that may contribute to both aging and disease.

The study – which was published in Nature Biotechnology – involved researchers from Insilico Medicine as well as Harvard Medical School, Stanford University, the Broad Institute, RWTH Aachen University, Peking University and Westlake University.
Study limitations
Zhavoronkov stressed that the findings are preliminary. "This is a pilot," he said. "It is early [and] exploratory."
The study had some limitations, including the small sample size – just 42 patients were analyzed over a 12-week period.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

The participants all had IPF, which can change many of the same proteins researchers use to measure biological aging. This means it’s possible that the improvements in the participants’ lung disease was related to the changes in blood proteins.

Larger and longer trials – including healthy older adults and populations without IPF – are needed to determine whether the drug truly has anti-aging effects and whether they could lead to better health. (iStock)
The findings don’t prove that the drug actually slows aging, keeps people healthier longer or extends their lives, the researchers acknowledged.
The results were based only on changes in proteins in their blood, and do not yet support the use of rentosertib as an anti-aging treatment.
Risks and side effects
The risks and side effects associated with rentosertib were found to be "manageable," according to Dr. Carol Ann Satler, senior vice president of clinical development for Insilico Medicine.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER
The most common potential side effects included mild diarrhea, slightly lower potassium levels in the blood and temporary increases in liver enzymes.
The drug was found to change patterns of proteins in the blood in ways that made patients appear an average of three to four years younger, in one case up to six years. (Insilico Medicine)
"Once you stop the drug, essentially, they return to normal," Satler told Fox News Digital.
In the next trial, the doctor said, "We'll be looking to adjust the doses of the drug based on the side effect profile so that people can stay on it longer."
Looking ahead
Rentosertib has now progressed into a year-long phase 3 study of more than 300 patients in China, according to Insilico.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Larger and longer trials – including healthy older adults and populations without IPF – are needed to determine whether the drug truly has anti-aging effects and whether they could lead to better health.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
While more research lies ahead, Zhavoronkov said the findings have given him more confidence to continue pursuing drugs that could target both age-related diseases and aging itself.
"Everybody agrees that living longer should be a fundamental human right for everyone," he said.
Melissa Rudy is senior health editor and a member of the lifestyle team at Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to melissa.rudy@fox.com.

title: 105-year-old credits ‘the good Lord’ for her long life: ‘Every day is a blessing’
summary: Blynda Vidock of Baytown, Texas, still lives independently at 105 and credits faith, athletics and eating well for her remarkable longevity and good health.
story: Dr. Annu Navani, chief medical officer at Le Reve Wellness, revelas why people should focus on adding healthy years to life — not chasing immortality.
A Texas woman who just turned 105 attributes her long life to "the good Lord."
While Blynda Vidock's faith may have played an important role in her longevity, the Baytown resident has also followed many of the habits that experts say can contribute to a longer, healthier life.

"The good Lord put me here for so many years, and it’s His life through me," she told FOX 26 Houston at her recent birthday celebration. "But I’ve always been very athletic, played tennis, swam all my life and ate good food."
GEORGIA WOMAN CELEBRATES 112TH BIRTHDAY, REVEALS HER SECRET TO A LONG LIFE
Vidock joked that she preaches to her children, grandchildren and "great-grands" to eat healthier, but said, "They still eat junk food!"
"We live faster nowadays," she said. "We used to have time to sit down and have a meal together."
Blynda Vidock celebrated more than a century of life with loved ones, joking at her birthday gathering that she had been made "queen for a day." (FOX 26 Houston KRIV)

Vidock was born in 1921 and grew up in West Palm Beach, Florida. While working for $15 a week at a bank in West Palm Beach, she crossed paths with big-name movie stars Clark Gable and Fred Astaire, and also recalled encountering a young John F. Kennedy.
She met Coast Guardsman Charles "Chuck" Vidock while volunteering with the USO during World War II. The two married and moved to Texas in 1946 and spent decades traveling the world together.
LONGEVITY DOCTOR REVEALS WHAT MATTERS MOST FOR AGING WELL, BEYOND PRICEY BIOHACKS
Vidock is "completely sharp, independent and full of stories from a century of living," according to the report.
A video from her birthday party shows the centenarian walking around and chatting animatedly with the many friends and family members who gathered to honor her.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"It’s wonderful to have you people here, and I don’t know if I’m supposed to dance or sing or get up on the table," she said. "I think I've been made queen for a day, and I've got my 15 minutes of fame, so you better enjoy it because it won't come again."
Every morning when she wakes up, Vidock said she wonders, "‘This is another day, Lord, why am I here?’" adding, "Every day is a blessing!"
Blynda Vidock celebrated her 105th birthday surrounded by friends and family in Texas. (FOX 26 Houston KRIV)
She said "the saddest part about getting old" is watching people lose their mental sharpness and credits "the good Lord" with allowing her to keep hers.
Vidock said a few simple habits have helped her live so long.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ
"Living like you know you’re supposed to live, being kind to people, and everything in moderation helped, and I got blessed with good genes, but then I took care of my body," she said.
Expert tips to improve healthspan

Dr. Annu Navani, chief medical officer at Le Reve Wellness in San Jose, California, recently told Fox News Digital that longevity medicine is more about adding life to years than adding years to life.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Rather than splurging on costly biohacks, procedures or supplements, Navani recommends focusing on simple daily practices that can enhance quality of life.
Getting high-quality sleep — about seven hours a night for the average person — is necessary for people to perform optimally and has been linked to a healthier lifespan, the expert said.
Regular exercise can support physical and mental health as people age, and may also help with stress management, experts say. (iStock)

Managing stress is another key factor in healthy aging, according to Navani. Regular physical activity and social interaction — two other factors linked to longevity — can also help people keep stress in check, as can regular meditation.

Eating a nutritious diet that includes a variety of vegetables, fruits, whole grains, protein and dairy, while limiting added sugars and ultraprocessed foods, is another important component of healthy aging.

Longevity experts David Cravit and Larry Wolf, authors of "The SuperAging Workbook," previously told Fox News Digital that maintaining a positive attitude is the No. 1 factor linked to living a longer life.

"People with a positive attitude outlive people with a negative attitude because it reduces stress, which, in turn, reduces inflammation, and inflammation is the cause of most age-related diseases," Cravit said.
The authors also recommended setting and working toward new goals, building strong relationships and maintaining a sense of independence as people age.
Melissa Rudy and Angelica Stabile of Fox News Digital contributed reporting.
Teresa Mull is a freelance writer with the Lifestyle team at Fox News Digital.

title: Libertarian tech mogul to hit DSA with an eight-figure spending nuke
summary: Scott Banister's $40 million funds Make Liberty Win's push to counter Democratic Socialists of America in state legislature races across nine states.
story: Tiffany Smiley, Endeavor PAC founder, warns the Democratic Party is too late to curb the far-left socialist movement. She asserts the party has accommodated radical ideas for over a year, with DSA-backed candidates winning nearly two dozen races. Smiley believes the Democratic Party has gone "off the tracks," making it difficult to regain control.
FIRST ON FOX — A wealthy tech investor is committing $40 million to help Republicans stem the tide of the Democratic Socialists of America in state-level races, Fox News Digital has learned.

Scott Banister, a libertarian who was an early investor in PayPal, Uber and SpaceX, among others, cut the massive check to Make Liberty Win, a right-of-center political organization. The funding has already been partially deployed in nine states — Wisconsin, Michigan, Minnesota, Pennsylvania, Georgia, Arizona, New Hampshire, West Virginia and Montana — with plans to expand the push to at least a dozen states.

"Self-described socialists are running for office and winning in the Democratic Party, like recently elected New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani," a press release obtained by Fox News Digital reads. "Make Liberty Win’s campaign will stem the tide of the far-left by mobilizing student and youth activists to knock on the doors of more than two million voters in key states."
SOCIALIST WINNING STREAK PUTS PRIZED DEMOCRATIC BATTLEGROUND AT RISK AS RADICAL LEFTISTS ADVANCE
Banister’s cash injection comes at an opportune time for Republicans.

Though Republicans enjoy a comfortable advantage at the national level, the Republican State Leadership Committee, the official GOP committee responsible for making sure the party wins at the state level, projected in late August that Democrats are slated to outspend Republicans in state races by a factor of three to one. Make Liberty Win’s spending could mitigate the liberals’ cash advantage.
Democrats have previously disputed claims that their state apparatus is better funded than the GOP’s.
NEW MIDTERM BATTLEGROUND TAKES SHAPE AS PARTIES BUILD ELECTION ARMIES
Members of the Democratic Socialists of America gather outside of a Trump owned building during a May Day rally in New York City in 2019. (Spencer Platt/Getty Images)
Make Liberty Win is a Republican-aligned political organization with a distinctly libertarian bent, supporting a smaller federal government and returning power to state legislatures.
It focuses on door knocking and phone banking on behalf of candidates, rather than giving money to them directly.
MUSK PICKS HIS FIRST GOP WARRIORS AS A 2026 MONEY SURGE TAKES SHAPE

Items on a table during an election night party held by the Democratic Socialists of America - LA chapter at The Greyhound on Tuesday, Nov. 4, 2025 in Los Angeles, CA (Eric Thayer / Los Angeles Times via Getty Images)

$40 million is a massive amount of money for any level of politics, especially state legislative races. For context, the average U.S. House candidate spent $1.8 million on a campaign in 2024 — and federal races are almost always more expensive than their state equivalents.

title: El-Sayed’s liberal agenda clashes with Muslim voters who back him anyway: ‘Male version’ of Ilhan Omar
summary: Muslim voters at an ISNA conference say they plan to back Abdul El-Sayed despite opposing his abortion and LGBTQ stances, citing Trump betrayals.
story: Muslim voters at the Islamic Society of North America's annual conference took issue with Abdul El-Sayed's positions on LGBTQ rights and abortion, but say that other issues motivate them to support him.

DETROIT, MICHIGAN — Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in Michigan, faces a striking disconnect among some Muslim voters who oppose his positions on abortion and LGBTQ issues yet say they plan to vote for him anyway.

"He is a Democrat with a Muslim mask," one attendee of the Islamic Society of North America (ISNA) Convention, who requested anonymity to avoid social reprisals, told Fox News Digital. "Basically he's like Ilhan Omar, but like a male version."
He went on to say that, while he takes objection to El-Sayed’s positions on abortion and LGBTQ rights, he "want[s] him to get elected" to improve his community’s "representation."

Fox News Digital was on the ground at the Islamic Society of North America’s annual conference in Detroit over Labor Day weekend, where El-Sayed delivered the marquee speech amid controversy over past remarks by some conference speakers. The episode has added scrutiny to El-Sayed’s ties to the organization and the political coalition surrounding his campaign.
‘DESTROYING THE AMERICAN WAY OF LIFE’: EL-SAYED’S POLITICAL ORBIT COMPLICATES EFFORT TO MODERATE HIS IMAGE
Abdul El-Sayed's campaign running a booth at the Islamic Society of North America's annual conference. (Robert Schmad/Fox News Digital) ((Robert Schmad/Fox News Digital))

In total, Fox News Digital spoke to about 10 attendees at the conference, some of whom requested anonymity or declined to be recorded but agreed to speak on background. Several described a tension between their personal views on social issues and their support for El-Sayed, particularly on abortion and LGBTQ issues.

El-Sayed supports codifying Roe v. Wade into law, funding Planned Parenthood, establishing LGBTQ-inclusive sex education and allowing doctors to perform sex-change operations on children. Islamic theology generally takes a more restrictive view of abortion, gender and sexuality, though interpretations vary among Muslims.

Another attendee, a Navy veteran, told Fox News Digital that he strongly opposes El-Sayed’s positions on issues like abortion and LGBTQ sex education, but feels like the Republican Party has let him down following the 2024 election.
"I voted for Donald Trump. When it comes to values, I'm a Republican. But unfortunately they have betrayed us," he said.

He pointed to the Trump administration’s involvement in foreign wars and cost-of-living concerns as the issues pushing him to support El-Sayed despite the Democrat’s liberal beliefs. Multiple attendees who spoke to Fox News Digital at the conference, including some who declined to be interviewed on the record, said they voted for Trump in 2024 but were planning on supporting El-Sayed in the midterms.
MICHIGAN SENATE RACE: EL-SAYED’S TIES TO EXTREMIST FUEL ANTISEMITISM CONCERNS AMONG JEWISH VOTERS
Abdul El-Sayed, a Democratic Senate candidate in Michigan, speaks to supporters at a campaign event, on August 2, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan (Paul Steinhauser/Fox News)

"We're concerned about where our tax dollars are going to. A lot of these tax dollars are going to support foreign wars, support countries that aren't the United States," Zubin, a long-time El-Sayed supporter, told Fox News Digital. "So I think these are the main issues that resonate not just with the Muslim voters but the everyday voter in all of Michigan."

President Donald Trump’s support for Israel and his military operations in Iran have become growing points of concern for some voters, with polls showing rising dissatisfaction over U.S. involvement in Middle Eastern conflicts.

Trump did uncharacteristically well for a Republican among Michigan Arab Americans in 2024. If support for the GOP slides heavily with that demographic in November, it could spell trouble for the party's Senate prospects. Republicans, however, are seeking to pick off disaffected Jewish Democrats to gain an edge themselves.
Some attendees who spoke with Fox News Digital were shocked to learn about El-Sayed’s support for abortion and LGBTQ rights.

"Wait, he's supporting LGBTQ?" one conference attendee, who requested to remain anonymous for social reasons, told Fox News Digital. "I don't really think that's good, especially because this is Islam and it prohibits LGBTQ and I do really think that people should abandon … abortion since they're taking a life away."
DETROIT VOTERS CALL ON DEMOCRATS TO UNITE AROUND EL-SAYED AFTER STUNNING VICTORY OF FAR-LEFT PROGRESSIVE

Abdul El-Sayed, a progressive candidate in the Democratic primary for U.S. Senate in Michigan, speaks during a primary election night event Wednesday, Aug. 5, 2026, at the Majestic Theatre in Detroit. (Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP Photo)

The attendee said he believes if El-Sayed’s social views were more widely known in the Islamic community, his support might decline. Others said they believe the importance of social views among Muslims is dependent on generation.

"So yes, Abdul El-Sayed, maybe his views when it comes to these things, maybe more similar to mine as compared to our parents, our grandparents, yes, with those generations. There may be a little bit of friction, but this is natural," Zubin said. "I do think, yes, these are probably going to be talking points within the Muslim community."

Some individuals who spoke to Fox News Digital acknowledged that the Islamic community has some deeply held conservative beliefs, but argued that the community will be able to look past that come November.

"He's gonna be great for education, and he's gonna be great for medical," Fauzi, who was attending the conference, told Fox News Digital. "5-10% of the issues, people may differ. But we have to look at the big picture [and] how he can be impactful for the state of Michigan, the country at large, and all of us here."
JEWISH DEM DEFECTIONS THREATEN EL-SAYED IN MICHIGAN SENATE RACE DECIDED BY RAZOR-THIN MARGINS
A speech being delivered at the Islamic Society of North America's annual conference. (Robert Schmad/Fox News Digital) ((Robert Schmad/Fox News Digital))

A handful of attendees who spoke with Fox News Digital said that their community would be excited if a Muslim Republican ran in their state, while others stressed that the party’s reputation could hamper its ability to appeal to Arab Americans.

"Yes, if you're a good person, a good politician and running for the Republican party and you believe in your values and that you can do good, go ahead and run and I'm sure you can win a lot of support from this community as well," Zubin said.

"I think it's very difficult for a Muslim to run as a Republican because frankly a lot of Republican voters do tend to have a strong bias against us," another attendee, who requested to remain anonymous, told Fox News Digital.

title: Unearthed clip shows Talarico calling parents 'abusive' for denying children's gender identity
summary: James Talarico, the Democratic Texas Senate candidate, once called parents' refusal to acknowledge a child's gender identity "abusive" behavior.
story: In a resurfaced 2019 video from his time as a state lawmaker, Talarico said parents who deny the gender of their child is "abusive for sure." (Credit: Texas House of Representatives)
James Talarico, the Democratic candidate for U.S. Senate in Texas, once described parents who refused to acknowledge their children’s gender identity as potentially engaging in "abusive" behavior.

"I think there are some folks that would think that if you deny your child's gender identity, that's incredibly harmful. And whether or not we label it with the term abuse, it's abusive for sure," Talarico said while speaking at a committee hearing in the Texas Legislature in 2019.

Talarico’s resurfaced comments add to a growing pile of past remarks that cut against his efforts to paint himself as a moderate on issues like gender, policing and border security as he attempts to win over Texas, a historically Republican-leaning state.
TALARICO SAYS HE 'MISSED THE MARK' AS HE BACKTRACKS ON CONTROVERSIAL WOKE STATEMENTS

Democratic U.S. Senate candidate James Talarico speaks during a campaign rally at the Cailloux Theater on Aug. 31, 2026, in Kerrville, Texas. Talarico is in a close race against Republican Ken Paxton ahead of the Nov. 3 general election. (Brandon Bell/Getty Images)
In the clip, Talarico had been speaking about HB 1910.
The legislation aimed to ensure that parents who refused to affirm their child’s gender identity would not be considered guilty of child abuse in cases deciding custody.

"In determining whether to appoint a party as a sole or joint managing conservator of a child, the court may not consider evidence regarding whether the party demonstrates a history or pattern of acknowledging or declining to acknowledge the child’s gender identity or expression," its text read.
Talarico opposed the bill, arguing that he would not rule out an overlap: that, in some cases, the lack of acknowledgment could border on abuse.
"My concern is ruling it out as not being abuse, I think, is dangerous and could certainly harm some of our most vulnerable kids in the state."
TALARICO CAMPAIGNS WITH SURGEON WHO OPERATED ON TRANSGENDER MINORS: ‘WOLF IN SHEEP’S CLOTHING’
State Rep. James Talarico during a Democratic primary debate at the Texas AFL-CIO COPE Convention in Georgetown, Texas, on Jan. 24, 2026. (Bob Daemmrich/The Texas Tribune/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

"Some of us I think really do consider this abusive behavior… an unwillingness to identify, acknowledge a child's gender identity. We consider that abusive to the child, abusive and destructive," Talarico said.
At least one Republican slammed Talarico's stance.

"Only perverts and pedophiles think about what is in little kids' pants as much as James Talafreako. He is a truly sick individual for dedicating his life to pushing sex changes on other people's kids," Zach Kraft, a spokesperson for the Republican National Committee (RNC), said in a statement to Fox News Digital.
Although that version of the bill died in committee, a later, stronger version of it eventually passed out of the Texas House in May 2025 and became law.
EXCLUSIVE: HOUSE COMMITTEE PROBES CHICAGO PUBLIC SCHOOLS OVER HIDING 'GENDER AFFIRMATION' FROM PARENTS
James Talarico speaks at a campaign event in Round Rock, Texas, on March 3, 2026. (Jordan Vonderhaar/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Talarico also opposed that version — one of 59 nay votes on the matter. Notably, Talarico also voted in favor of an amendment to sunset the law in 2030 and in support of a separate amendment clarifying that, in the words of its author, "rejecting a child's gender identity or sexual orientation is abuse" and "should be treated as such under Texas law."

When asked about the bill and his statements in committee, the Talarico campaign said he supported and respected parental decisions about their children.

"James believes parents have the most important say in decisions about their children, which is why he sponsored a bill to protect parental rights and ensure parents are responsible for the upbringing of their own kids. While James has fought for Texas parents and families, Ken Paxton has endangered them by allowing pedophiles back on our streets," JT Ennis, a spokesperson for the Talarico campaign, said in a statement to Fox News Digital.
Leo Briceno is a politics reporter for the congressional team at Fox News Digital. He was previously a reporter with World Magazine.

title: DSA-backed candidates are winning primaries and their vision for America is very different
summary: Democratic Socialists of America launched its "Workers Deserve More" program calling for public ownership, a 32-hour workweek and universal healthcare.
story: NYC-DSA co-chair Grace Mausser argues that capitalism is failing many Americans who cannot afford housing, childcare or education. She advocates for economic populism and draws lessons from successful policies in American history, such as the New Deal, as well as those implemented in other countries. Mausser stresses the need for policies like universal healthcare.

The Democratic Socialists of America is seeking to reshape some of the most basic features of the U.S. economy — from who owns major corporations to how long Americans work and whether families pay for healthcare, college and housing.

The agenda is drawing renewed scrutiny after DSA-backed candidates gained ground in the 2026 midterm primaries and progressive socialism became a central Republican target at the GOP's first-ever midterm convention in Dallas.
Below are some of the biggest economic proposals in the platform.
Public ownership of major corporations and industries
The Democratic Socialists of America says major corporations and key industries should be publicly owned rather than privately controlled. (Spencer Platt/Getty Images)
DSA calls for public ownership of major corporations and essential industries, arguing public ownership would give Americans greater democratic control over the economy.
Adam Lehodey, a policy expert at the Manhattan Institute, said nationalizing major corporations would cost billions of dollars and shift accountability from customers to government officials.
'WASTEFUL DISTRACTION': EXPERTS SLAM MAMDANI'S TAXPAYER-FUNDED STORES
He argued nationalized industries have historically suffered from waste, corruption and lower productivity, adding that reducing regulations would be a better way to encourage competition.
A 32-hour workweek with full pay
The Democratic Socialists of America says full-time employees should work 32 hours a week without a reduction in pay or benefits. (iStock)
DSA also wants to establish a 32-hour workweek without reducing workers' pay or benefits, effectively giving full-time employees an additional day away from work while preserving their compensation.
The proposal is paired with a living minimum wage, paid family leave and stronger protections for workers to form unions and strike.
TRUMP DANGLES $5,000 CHECKS AS DEBT SURGES — BUT ONLY IF GOP CAN CLEAR MAJOR MIDTERM HURDLE
The agenda does not explain how a shorter workweek would be implemented across industries or how businesses would be expected to absorb the additional labor costs.
Lehodey said a 32-hour workweek without higher productivity could increase labor costs and reduce economic output.
Universal healthcare, housing and education
The Democratic Socialists of America says healthcare should be provided at no cost to individuals. (iStock)
Among DSA's biggest proposals are universal healthcare, publicly owned social housing, free public education through college and cancellation of all student debt.
Together, the proposals would shift a much larger share of healthcare, housing and education costs from individuals to the federal government.

A Cato Institute analysis estimated that a "Medicare-for-all"-style healthcare system alone could increase federal spending by between $40 trillion and $75 trillion over a decade, though the estimate is not specific to DSA's proposal.
Higher taxes on wealthy Americans and corporations
DSA's platform calls for higher taxes on wealthy Americans and corporations to help fund its broader economic agenda. (Spencer Platt/Getty Images)
DSA says wealthy Americans and large corporations should shoulder more of the cost of its vision.
The platform calls for "aggressive wealth taxes" on the richest individuals and corporations, with the proceeds directed toward public goods and infrastructure.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Lehodey questioned whether wealthy taxpayers alone could finance the agenda, arguing a broader group of taxpayers would likely bear some of the cost.
DSA's platform does not estimate the total cost of its agenda or how much revenue its proposed tax increases would generate.
Amanda Macias covers the intersection of business, economics and politics, with a focus on how policy decisions shape markets, businesses and American workers.

title: Trump touts White House renovations, says building was in ‘very bad condition’
summary: President Donald Trump said the White House looked like a "dump" before his renovations, saying the exterior skin was "practically falling off."
story: President Donald Trump showed reporters construction outside the White House, announcing a variety of new upgrades.
President Donald Trump on Sunday touted new renovations to the White House, saying the building was a "dump" before the updates.
In a post on Truth Social, Trump said the White House was in "very bad condition" and that previous administrations failed to take proper care of it.

"The White House was in very bad condition, both inside and out. Frankly, it was a 'dump!' Past Presidents did not take care of it," Trump wrote. "I love renovating it during my spare time, which is not much."
TRUMP'S WHITE HOUSE BALLROOM CONSTRUCTION GETS ANOTHER LIFELINE FROM SCOTUS AMID HEATED LEGAL FIGHT
President Donald Trump boasted about new renovations to the White House. (Getty Images:Truth Social/DonaldTrump)
He added that the Department of the Interior and various contractors are doing a "fantastic job" with the renovations.
"The exterior 'skin' of the Building was practically falling off! It is now in better shape than when built in 1792. Such an Honor to have the privilege of saving this Great Structure!" Trump wrote.
The president said that more time without a renovation would have "destroyed our beloved White House!"
President Donald Trump said the White House was in "very bad condition" and that previous administrations failed to take proper care of it. (Truth Social/Donald Trump)

This comes amid several structural and aesthetic changes Trump has pursued at the White House that have drawn criticism from some preservationists and legal challenges, including fortifying the North Portico entrance, adding gold ornamentation to the Oval Office and Cabinet Room, paving over the historic Rose Garden and demolishing the East Wing to make room for a planned 90,000-square-foot ballroom.

The administration has also made major changes to other structures in Washington, including renovating the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, proposing to repaint the Eisenhower Executive Office Building and undertaking extensive renovations at the Kennedy Center.

title: Federal judge rules Trump admin plan to cut FEMA workforce in half is unlawful
summary: A federal judge ruled DHS unlawfully seized the Federal Emergency Management Agency's authority over staffing and pushed thousands of job cuts.
story: Chief legal correspondent Shannon Bream details the Supreme Court's latest rulings, including a decision in Trump v. Slaughter affirming the president's power to dismiss a Federal Trade Commission commissioner. However, in Trump v. Cook, the court states the president cannot unilaterally fire a Federal Reserve governor. These opinions shape executive power and independent agencies.
A federal judge ruled that the Trump administration's directive for the Federal Emergency Management Agency to cut its workforce in half was unlawful.

U.S. District Judge Susan Illston found on Friday that the Department of Homeland Security acted unlawfully by taking control of FEMA's authority over its own personnel and pushing the agency to slash thousands of disaster-response jobs.

Although FEMA is under DHS, a federal law adopted after Hurricane Katrina in 2005 states that the department "may not substantially or significantly reduce (FEMA's) authorities, responsibilities, or functions."
Illston said the department violated the law last year when it sought to stop FEMA from renewing the temporary contracts of thousands of on-call reservists who respond to disasters.
DHS PLANS COSTLY CRACKDOWN ON STATES THAT DON’T COOPERATE ON ELECTION SECURITY
A federal judge ruled that the Trump administration's order for the Federal Emergency Management Agency to cut its workforce in half was unlawful. (Kevin Carter/Getty Images)
"There is no evidence in the record reflecting reasoned decision-making for this about-face or for the subsequent conditions DHS placed on FEMA’s renewal authority," Illston wrote.
Illston's ruling did not include remedies or penalties, noting that those would be addressed in a separate ruling next month.
The judge said the parties have until Oct. 9 to submit briefings on "what relief remains outstanding" in this case.

The unions that sued argued that the planned cuts are unlawful because they would undermine FEMA's core disaster‑response mission, were not approved by Congress and were ordered by then-Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem instead of FEMA officials.
President Donald Trump has suggested that FEMA should ​be eliminated and that states ⁠should handle their emergency preparedness. (Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images)

The administration has contended that FEMA has considerable flexibility to determine proper staffing levels. President Donald Trump has suggested that FEMA should ​be eliminated and that states ⁠should handle their emergency preparedness.
In June, Illston declined to immediately block the job cuts, ruling that FEMA had at least temporarily abandoned its planned layoffs.

But on Friday, the judge wrote that FEMA appeared to be moving forward with the job cuts. She said FEMA projected its staffing levels for the upcoming fiscal year at 11,383 employees, or about half of previous levels, without any basis for picking that figure.
DEM GOV LASHES OUT AS TRUMP HUD SCRUTINIZES NEARLY $2B IN DISASTER FUNDS OVER FRAUD CONCERNS

The unions that sued argued that the planned cuts are unlawful because they would undermine FEMA's core disaster‑response mission, were not approved by Congress and were ordered by then-Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem instead of FEMA officials. (Al Drago/Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Fox News Digital reached out to DHS and FEMA for comment but they did not immediately respond.

"Under President Trump and [DHS] Secretary [Markwayne] Mullin’s leadership, DHS and FEMA are ready for the 2026 hurricane season," a FEMA spokesperson said in a statement to The Hill. "FEMA continues to maintain a roster of experienced leadership and support staff across headquarters and regional offices. No position is without experienced leadership."
In a separate ruling, the judge also faulted FEMA and DHS officials for using the Signal messaging app on their personal cellphones to discuss staffing cuts and deleting the messages.

Illston said the messages would have been relevant to the lawsuit and that she would now presume "that the lost Signal messages would have been unfavorable to Defendants because they would have been further evidence" of unlawful conduct.
Reuters contributed to this report.

title: Trump says China 'spies' on US after report ties Chinese imagery to Iran strike
summary: The president said the U.S. spies on China "too" after a report linked Chinese satellite imagery to Iran's deadly July missile attack on American troops.
story: Rep. Claudia Tenney, R-N.Y., discusses President Donald Trump’s prediction that the Iran war will end after the 2026 midterm elections on ‘Fox Report.’

President Donald Trump said Sunday that China "spies on us" just as "we spy on them," following a report that Chinese entities provided Iran with satellite imagery before a deadly missile attack that killed three U.S. troops.

While speaking to reporters aboard Air Force One, Trump was asked about a Wall Street Journal report that Chinese entities allegedly supplied Iran with high-resolution satellite imagery of Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan before Tehran's July 17 missile attack.
"They basically do what we do," Trump said.
TRUMP GIVES SMITHSONIAN DAYS TO REPLACE 'STRANGE MODERNIST SCULPTURE' WITH FOUNDING FATHER
President Donald Trump said Sunday that China "spies on us" and that "we spy on them too." (Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP)
Asked whether he planned to raise the issue with Chinese President Xi Jinping when he visits the U.S., Trump said Xi has "behaved reasonably well," and that "we behave reasonably well."
"You know what they say? That China spies on us. I say you're right, and we spy on them, too," Trump said.
TRUMP TELLS ZELENSKYY TO STOP DOING 'ONE THING' DURING ATTACKS ON RUSSIA
U.S. officials have reportedly linked the imagery to Iran's July 17 strike on the Jordanian base, which killed three U.S. troops. (Spencer Platt/Getty Images)

Chinese President Xi Jinping is scheduled to visit Washington on Sept. 24 for a summit with Trump. (Szilard Koszticsak/MTI via AP)
The U.S. officials did not identify the Chinese entities involved or accuse Beijing of direct involvement in the attack.

title: Trump unloads on AOC, Mamdani for laughing during sacred 9/11 ceremony at Ground Zero
summary: President Donald Trump called the moment "terrible" after video showed AOC and Zohran Mamdani appearing to laugh during the Ground Zero ceremony.
story: President Donald Trump says it was "inappropriate" for Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani to be laughing during a 9/11 memorial ceremony.

President Donald Trump slammed Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani for appearing to laugh during the solemn reading of victims’ names at the 9/11 Memorial, calling their behavior "terrible" and "inappropriate."
"I think it’s terrible," Trump said when asked about the video of the two Democrats. "It’s not a place to be laughing, especially in that case."
"I thought it was terrible," he continued. "The fact that they were laughing together at a very important part of the ceremony was inappropriate."
The president’s condemnation came after video of Ocasio-Cortez and Mamdani sharing what appeared to be a lighthearted exchange at Ground Zero sparked widespread criticism online.
AOC, MAMDANI INTERACTION CAUGHT ON CAM AT 9/11 MEMORIAL SPARKS ONLINE FURY
Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., left, and Mayor Zohran Mamdani, right, appear to laugh during the reading-of-names at the 9/11 Memorial. (Screenshot/Fox News)

A television feed from Friday’s ceremony showed a young man overcome with emotion near the memorial before cutting to Mamdani and Ocasio-Cortez smiling and appearing to laugh as they spoke. Their conversation could not be heard.
9/11 WIDOW TERRY STRADA ACCUSES US OF PROTECTING SAUDI ARABIA 25 YEARS AFTER TERROR ATTACKS, ADDRESSES VANCE

Representative Alexandria Ocasio Cortez, a Democrat from New York, center, and Zohran Mamdani, mayor of New York, center right, during the 25th anniversary commemoration ceremony at the National 9/11 Memorial and Museum in New York. ( )

The moment unfolded as mourners read aloud the names of those killed in the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks and the 1993 World Trade Center bombing during ceremonies marking the 25th anniversary of 9/11. Nearly 3,000 people were killed in the 2001 attacks.
The video quickly spread across social media, where critics accused the pair of showing disrespect on one of the nation’s most solemn days.
MAMDANI DRAWS FURY FROM 9/11 MOURNERS OVER GROUND ZERO APPEARANCE: ‘DISRESPECTFUL’
Colorful flowers are left by mourners at the 911 Memorial, offering gifts to remember those killed in the September 11 terrorist attacks on New York City. (Getty)
"As the names of Americans murdered on September 11th are read aloud at Ground Zero, AOC and Mamdani are laughing and smiling together," Rep. Wesley Hunt, R-Texas, wrote on X.
"There is a time and a place for politics. This isn’t it. Ground Zero is sacred ground," Hunt added. "September 11 is not a photo op, it is not a networking event."
MAMDANI HEADS TO 9/11 MEMORIAL DESPITE 110,000-SIGNATURE PUSH FROM VICTIMS’ FAMILIES TO STAY AWAY
Meghan McCain also reacted to the video, asking on X, "Why the f--- are these two laughing?"
New York City Councilwoman Inna Vernikov, a Republican, similarly ripped the moment.
ZOHRAN MAMDANI URGED TO SKIP NEW YORK CITY'S 9/11 MEMORIAL: 'VILE ANTISEMITE'
"After thousands of families of victims of terror beg Mamdani not to show up, he stands there and laughs while families weep," Vernikov wrote. "This is NYC’s Mayor."

Mamdani had already faced opposition from some victims’ families ahead of the ceremony. A petition urging him to stay away from Ground Zero gathered more than 110,000 signatures, though Mamdani attended and remained for the ceremony.
DE NIRO CALLS CONTROVERSIAL MAMDANI POLICE COMMENTS 'RIDICULOUS' AS HE DEFENDS MAYOR GOING TO 9/11 SERVICE

Flowers and American flags rest beside inscribed names at a reflecting pool at the National September 11 Memorial & Museum on Sept. 11, 2026, in New York City, as the nation commemorated the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 terrorist attacks. (Jeenah Moon - Pool/Getty Images)
However, Michael Ragusa, who has served as a member of former New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani’s entourage, disputed claims that Mamdani and Ocasio-Cortez were joking about the ceremony.
"The videos of [them] laughing are not true. I was standing next to them the whole time," Ragusa wrote on X.
MS RACHEL DEFENDS 'AWESOME' MAMDANI AMID 9/11 MEMORIAL CONTROVERSY, SAYS HE'S VICTIM OF ISLAMOPHOBIC ATTACKS
"The camera just caught her greeting him hello," he added. "Multiple other politicians were laughing and joking behind me. Republicans and Democrats."
Mamdani was seen standing somberly at other points during the ceremony. It remains unclear what he and Ocasio-Cortez discussed during the brief exchange.

title: GOP gov candidate recounts miracle water landing as dispatch audio reveals desperate search for sinking plane
summary: Dispatch audio captures the frantic search for Tom Tiffany after his plane lost power and plunged into Lake Wausau in darkness Saturday night.
story: Dispatch audio captures the frantic search for Wisconsin GOP gubernatorial candidate Tom Tiffany and his pilot after their plane lost power and sank in Lake Wausau. (Audio provided by Broadcastify)

A desperate search unfolded across a dark Wisconsin lake after Republican gubernatorial candidate Tom Tiffany’s powerless plane plunged into the water and disappeared beneath the surface with rescuers unsure where he and his pilot had gone.
Dramatic dispatch audio captures crews calling for more ambulances, engines and boats as they raced to find the two men and tracked the last GPS location of a phone believed to be underwater.
"We’re going to be in search for a down plane," one responder warned.
WISCONSIN GOP GOVERNOR CANDIDATE SWIMS FROM SINKING PLANE AFTER EMERGENCY LAKE LANDING
First responders gather near a Lake Wausau boat landing during the rescue of Wisconsin gubernatorial candidate Tom Tiffany and his pilot. (WSAW)
Hours after leaving the hospital, Tiffany revealed Sunday that pilot Leonard "Len" Boltz had just seconds to react after the plane lost power on its final approach to Wausau Downtown Airport.
"Len said to me, ‘We are going down. Pull your seatbelt tight,’" Tiffany recalled during a news conference. "And that’s exactly what I did. I gave it a yank and pulled it good and tight."
COAST GUARD PLANE WITH DHS SECRETARY MARKWAYNE MULLIN ON BOARD MAKES EMERGENCY LANDING AFTER ENGINE FAILURE
Emergency crews search Lake Wausau after a plane carrying Wisconsin GOP gubernatorial candidate Tom Tiffany lost power and landed in the water. (WSAW)
"It was probably about 10 seconds later," he added. "We hit the water."
The impact sent Tiffany’s head into the dashboard, leaving him with a gash above his right eye that required 12 stitches. Boltz received four stitches for one of his injuries, Tiffany said.
PILOT'S BRAVERY ON DISPLAY IN STEERING CRIPPLED PLANE CLEAR OF TRAGEDY IN DRAMATIC WATER LANDING
The two men checked on each other before escaping through the passenger-side door as the plane began filling with water.
Tiffany searched the cockpit for his phone but could not find it. Boltz still had his phone and called 911.
PILOT DECLARES MAYDAY BEFORE SEAPLANE COMES DOWN IN NEW YORK CITY’S EAST RIVER
They climbed atop the slowly sinking plane and waited there for roughly 10 minutes as emergency lights appeared around the lake.

As the aircraft slipped underwater beneath them, they began swimming toward the airport. They made it roughly 100 to 150 feet before Tiffany reached a high spot in the lake where the water was about five feet deep.
MULTIPLE INJURED AFTER FLOATPLANE MAKES EMERGENCY LANDING, CATCHES FIRE OFF WASHINGTON COAST
FILE - Rep. Tom Tiffany was taken to the hospital after the small plane lost power and crashed into a lake. (Mark Schiefelbein-Pool/Getty Images)
"I said to Len, ‘Let’s just stay right here until help can come,’ because we could see the sirens," Tiffany said.
His voice cracked as the gravity of the ordeal appeared to catch up with him.
"We are just really fortunate," Tiffany said, pausing as he became emotional. "We’re really fortunate that God was looking after us last night."
The dispatch audio revealed the uncertainty confronting first responders as they raced toward different points along Lake Wausau.
"Can you get another ambulance rolling this way and one more engine, please?" one responder said. "Also page SAFER mutual aid to Bluegill Park with a boat."
Another responder reported that a witness had seen the aircraft go down but could provide only a general search area.
"I’m on scene with the reporting party," the responder said. "He stated he did see [an] aircraft crash."
4 FLORIDA FAMILY MEMBERS FOUND DEAD AFTER SMALL PLANE GOES DOWN OFF THE BAHAMAS
Crews carried thermal-imaging equipment and used a phone’s last known GPS coordinates to narrow the search. A landowner also provided a boat for deputies to use, according to the radio traffic.
"I was talking to the pilots," a responder said. "It sounds like they may plan to swim to the nearest shore after it went under, and then I lost contact with them."
"I believe his phone is underwater," he added. "They may be swimming south, I believe."
The tense search ended when rescuers announced that both men had been located.
"We have two victims in the water," a responder said. "We’re just pulling them out now."
Minutes later, a crew reported both were "alert, conscious" and confirmed everyone aboard the aircraft had been accounted for.
FILE - Republican U.S. Rep. Tom Tiffany, a candidate for Wisconsin governor, said he received stiches following the crash. (AP Photo/Scott Bauer)

Tiffany credited Boltz’s experience with keeping the emergency landing from becoming deadly. The former Air Force pilot trainer raised the plane’s landing gear before touching down, preventing it from potentially cartwheeling across the water.
"He was savvy enough and quick enough to think about, ‘We’ve got to make sure and pull that landing gear up,’" Tiffany said. "He did that, and it might have saved us."
Tiffany estimated the plane was still traveling between 70 and 80 mph when it hit the lake, describing the impact as "a fast-moving car crash."
"We’re fortunate the plane didn’t flip," he said. "I just take that to the skill of the pilot."
Wausau Mayor Doug Diny, a former military pilot, also praised Boltz for safely bringing the aircraft down at night.
PILOT RESCUED AFTER WORLD WAR II-ERA PLANE CRASHES AT PENNSYLVANIA AIRPORT
FILE - Republican Rep. Tom Tiffany of Wisconsin, a GOP gubernatorial candidate, said he plans to return to the campaign trail Monday. (Paul Steinhauser/Fox News)
"The last thing anyone wants to do as a pilot is put the aircraft in the water at night," Diny said.

Tiffany and Boltz were taken to Aspirus Wausau Hospital and released after treatment. Tiffany said a CT scan found no apparent concussion, though doctors instructed him to watch for possible symptoms and avoid flying for several days.
Despite canceling a trip to Washington, D.C., Tiffany said he plans to return to the campaign trail Monday.
"This will not deter me in my efforts that I started a year ago to become the next governor of the state of Wisconsin," he said.
The single-engine Beechcraft Bonanza remained submerged Sunday. The Federal Aviation Administration is investigating what caused it to lose power.
House Speaker Mike Johnson celebrated Tiffany’s return following the close call.
"Grateful to God no one was hurt in this accident and my good friend @TomTiffanyWI is safe and back on the trail!" Johnson wrote on X.
Tiffany represents Wisconsin’s 7th Congressional District and is running against Democratic Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley in November.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Crowley said he was grateful Tiffany and the pilot survived and praised Boltz’s actions.
Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.

title: Trump says Lindsay Clancy case is a ‘state situation' following attorney's pardon plea
summary: President Donald Trump expressed sympathy for the family of Lindsay Clancy’s three children while signaling that he would not intervene in the former nurse’s state murder case.
story: Retired Massachusetts Superior Court Judge Jack Lu told Fox News Digital a plea deal would be a "good idea" and in the public's "interest," but predicted prosecutors will again seek a first-degree murder conviction.

President Donald Trump on Sunday signaled that he would not intervene in the case of Massachusetts mother Lindsay Clancy, who is charged with killing her three young children amid allegations that she suffered from postpartum psychosis.
When asked whether he would pardon Clancy, Trump called the situation "very sad" but said the case is ultimately a "state situation," not a federal one.
"There’s no winner there. There’s no win no matter what you do. Three children are dead," he said.
LINDSAY CLANCY'S LAWYER REVEALS POST-MISTRIAL STRATEGY AS RETRIAL LOOMS
FILE — Trump expressed sympathy for the children’s deaths but said Clancy’s defense and the prosecution must resolve the case at the state level. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

The response came after Kevin Reddington, who represents Clancy, publicly asked Trump to grant his client a pardon last week. Reddington had acknowledged that Trump had no authority to issue a pardon in a state matter, but hoped he could still influence the outcome, according to his interview with WBZ-TV.
Trump indicated that the defense and prosecution need to resolve the legal matter at the local level while praising Reddington's work.
"He’s a good attorney. I’ve heard from other people he’s a very good attorney," Trump said. "I hope they can work it out. That’s something they have to work out … There is no win there."
LINDSAY CLANCY JUROR ADMITTED 'REASONABLE DOUBT' BUT STILL REFUSED INSANITY VERDICT, FOREPERSON SAYS
Lindsay Clancy arrives at court after being charged with three counts of first-degree murder in the deaths of her three children. (Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger via AP, Pool)
Previously, Trump said Clancy would still have to "pay the price" for the deaths of her three children.

"I assume there's going to be another trial. It's a terrible situation. Look, she did a horrible, horrible thing. Can't be worse. But you'll find out what the price to pay is. There'll be a price. It's going to be [a] mental institution or jail or something," he said.
Clancy, a 36-year-old former nurse, faces three counts of first-degree murder in the 2023 deaths of her children: 5-year-old Cora, 3-year-old Dawson and 8-month-old Callan.
After their deaths, Clancy attempted to kill herself and was left paralyzed from the injuries.
Her defense attorneys have argued that Clancy suffered from postpartum psychosis, a severe but rare psychiatric condition that causes a sudden loss of reality after childbirth.

According to ABC, Reddington said Clancy had sought treatment from a psychiatrist he described as inexperienced. The psychiatrist reportedly prescribed her medications for postpartum depression in the months leading up to her reported psychotic break.
Callan, left, Dawson and Cora Clancy are pictured in an undated photo. The three children were killed at their home in Duxbury, Massachusetts, in January 2023. (Lindsay Marie Clancy/Facebook)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Clancy now faces a potential retrial after jurors deadlocked following a full week of deliberations, prompting Judge William Sullivan to declare a mistrial earlier this month.
The jury was split 11 to 1, with 11 jurors reportedly favoring an acquittal on the grounds that Clancy was not criminally responsible for the killings. The jury consisted of nine women and three men.
Fox News Digital’s Michael Ruiz and Elaine Mallon contributed to this report.
Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

title: Trump tells Zelenskyy to stop doing 'one thing' during attacks on Russia
summary: President Donald Trump told reporters he wants Volodymyr Zelensky to stop hitting Russian diesel refineries, saying the strikes are causing a global fuel shortage.
story: President Donald Trump has a blunt message for Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy as Kyiv continues targeting Russia: Stop hitting its diesel refineries.
President Donald Trump has a blunt message for Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy as Kyiv continues targeting Russia: Stop hitting its diesel refineries.

Trump made the remarks Sunday while attending the Irish Open at his golf club in Doonbeg, Ireland, after a reporter asked whether he had spoken with Zelenskyy following a recent conversation with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
"Zelensky has to do one thing. He has to stop knocking out diesel fuel in Russia," Trump told reporters.
TRUMP NEGOTIATORS WITKOFF, KUSHNER MEET WITH PUTIN IN MOSCOW AS US PUSHES FOR END TO RUSSIA-UKRAINE WAR
FILE - President Donald Trump said he spoke with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky about the issue, noting there are other targets the country could focus on. (Getty Images)
Trump said Ukraine could continue pursuing other targets inside Russia but urged Zelenskyy to steer clear of the country’s diesel infrastructure.
"Let him go after targets, but not diesel fuel because he's causing a shortage of diesel," Trump said. "This isn't done by the Middle East. This is done by what's happening with Russia and Ukraine."
The president said he had already spoken directly with Zelenskyy about the issue.

"So we spoke to Mr. Zelensky about it. There are plenty of other targets," Trump said. "Don't hit diesel fuel because that's hurting the world. We don't want him to hit diesel fuel. He's hitting diesel refineries."
FILE - Trump said the military strikes are exacerbating a global diesel shortage. (Joe Raedle/Getty Images)
WATCH: FIGHTS BREAK OUT AT RUSSIAN GAS STATIONS AS PUTIN ADMITS FUEL SHORTAGES

Trump’s remarks come as Ukraine has targeted Russia’s oil and gas infrastructure with long-range strikes, part of Kyiv’s effort to hamper an industry that provides revenue and fuel for Moscow’s war effort. Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine more than four years ago.

The strikes have put pressure on Russia’s fuel supplies, prompting rationing in parts of the country and a Russian ban on diesel exports in July. The disruption has also added pressure to global diesel supplies, which have faced additional strain amid reduced oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz.
Diesel prices in the U.S. climbed above an average of $6 per gallon on Friday, reaching a record high.
FILE - Diesel prices reached a record high in the U.S. on Friday. (Rebecca Noble/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
Russia has intensified its aerial attacks on Ukraine in recent weeks, including strikes involving ballistic missiles and drones, while Ukraine has continued targeting sites inside Russia.

Russian and Ukrainian officials reported another round of large-scale drone attacks overnight into Sunday, with casualties reported on both sides.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: Election chaos in this red state just got even stranger for Republicans after Supreme Court ruling
summary: The Supreme Court blocked Missouri's new congressional map, forcing the state to use 2022 boundaries that favor Emanuel Cleaver's Kansas City district.
story: A major midterm shakeup unfolds as the Missouri Supreme Court blocks the state's new congressional map despite its use in primaries where over 1.2 million citizens voted. Missouri Gov. Mike Kehoe joins 'Fox & Friends' to discuss the ruling, which President Trump called a 'dark day.'
Republicans suffered a fresh blow in Missouri after the Supreme Court blocked a congressional map that could have helped the GOP gain another House seat in November.
The ruling, handed down last week, means Missouri will use its 2022 congressional map instead of the new boundaries backed by President Donald Trump and Missouri Republicans.

Missouri held its August primary under the new map, meaning candidates won their party nominations based on one set of district boundaries. But those boundaries will change before the November election, when Missouri is expected to return to its 2022 map.
TRUMP DANGLES $5,000 CHECKS AS DEBT SURGES — BUT ONLY IF GOP CAN CLEAR MAJOR MIDTERM HURDLE
People opposed to a congressional redistricting plan rally outside the Missouri Capitol in Jefferson City, Mo., Wednesday, Sept. 2, 2026. (AP Photo/David A. Lieb)

Typically, states redraw their congressional and state legislative districts once every decade after the Census to account for population changes and ensure that each district has roughly the same number of residents.
The new map would have shifted parts of Democratic Rep. Emanuel Cleaver’s Kansas City district into more Republican-leaning areas, making the seat more competitive.

Republicans hoped the changes would help them win seven of Missouri’s eight House seats in the November midterm elections. The GOP currently holds six of the state’s eight seats, while Democrats hold two.
Missouri must now use the 2022 map, which keeps Cleaver’s district more favorable to Democrats.

The maps show how Missouri’s congressional districts changed between 2022 and 2025, including the expansion of the Kansas City-area 5th District into more Republican-leaning rural parts of the state. (Missouri Office of Administration/Amanda Macias/Fox News Digital)
The Supreme Court’s decision came after more than a year of legal battles over which congressional map Missouri should use.

Missouri held its August primary under the new map, but the state will use its 2022 district boundaries for the November general election. That means some voters could be assigned to a different congressional district in November than the one in which they voted during the primary.
The change could affect more than 1 million voters, or nearly one-fourth of Missouri’s electorate, according to an Associated Press estimate.
The conflicting court orders have added to the confusion, with the November election just weeks away. Candidates and election officials must now adjust to the 2022 boundaries.
MISSOURI HIGH COURT BLOCKS GOP-BACKED CONGRESSIONAL MAPS AHEAD OF MIDTERMS; TRUMP BLASTS 'RIDICULOUS' RULING
The Supreme Court blocked Missouri from using a GOP-backed congressional map that could have helped Republicans gain a House seat in November. (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images)
The Supreme Court did not explain its reasoning in the brief order.

The White House did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment.
Amanda Macias covers the intersection of business, economics and politics, with a focus on how policy decisions shape markets, businesses and American workers.

title: Trump gives Smithsonian days to replace 'strange modernist sculpture' with Founding Father
summary: President Donald Trump demands a 30-foot George Washington statue replace the "Infinity" sculpture outside the National Museum of American History in Washington.
story: 'The Ingraham Angle' host Laura Ingraham exposes how progressive curators inside the Smithsonian are rewriting American history through radical exhibitions. Historian Dr. Jody Edward Ginn analyzes the systemic exclusion of conservative perspectives, noting that a new exhibit features three times more liberal items than conservative ones.
President Donald Trump is calling on the Smithsonian to replace a decades-old modernist sculpture outside the National Museum of American History with a towering, 30-foot statue of George Washington.

In social media posts late Friday, Trump said the "Infinity" sculpture that has stood outside the museum since 1967 "says nothing about America," while Washington, he argued, "more than anyone else, says everything about America."
Trump also called for the museum to open a five-year exhibition honoring Washington that would run through Feb. 22, 2032, the 300th anniversary of the first president’s birth.
INSIDE THE BEHEMOTH SMITHSONIAN MUSEUM NETWORK DRAWING FIRE FROM THE TRUMP ADMINISTRATION
People walking past the "Infinity" sculpture outside the Smithsonian National Museum of American History on the National Mall in Washington Tuesday, Sept. 8, 2026. (AP Photo/Pablo Martinez Monsivais)

Trump also wants the Smithsonian to install an 11-foot statue of Washington in the museum’s Flag Hall by Constitution Day on Sept. 17. The statue was featured at the recent Freedom 250 Grand Prix race.
"Immediately design and display a five-year exhibition worthy of the Life, Sacrifice, and Contributions of George Washington," Trump wrote.
"Then, as soon as it is ready, install a 30-foot Washington Colossus where ‘Infinity’ stands today."
"Infinity," created by New York artist José de Rivera, was commissioned by the federal government and installed outside the museum in 1967.

President Donald Trump has argued the Smithsonian should place greater emphasis on America's founding principles, national achievements and patriotic history. (Maxine Wallace/The Washington Post/Getty Images)

It is unclear whether Trump can order the Smithsonian to make the changes. The institution is outside the executive branch and is overseen by a Board of Regents that includes Vice President JD Vance, Chief Justice John Roberts, lawmakers from both parties and citizen members.
Fox News Digital reached out to the Smithsonian for comment but did not immediately receive a response.
Trump has repeatedly criticized how the Smithsonian presents American history, particularly as the country celebrates its 250th anniversary.
EXCAVATION SET TO BEGIN ON TRUMP ADMINISTRATION'S 250-FOOT TRIUMPHAL ARCH AMID LEGAL BATTLE
In his posts Friday, he accused the National Museum of American History of giving too little attention to Washington and other Founding Fathers.
Trump singled out Washington’s crossing of the Delaware River on Christmas night in 1776 and the American victory at Trenton, saying the museum does not give those events the attention they deserve.

This painting, "Washington Crossing the Delaware" (by Emanuel Leutze, American, 1816-1868), 1851, shows George Washington's crossing of the Delaware River on the night of December 25-26, 1776, as part of a surprise sneak attack on the British Army during the American Revolutionary War. (GraphicaArtis via Getty Images)
"He is easily America’s Greatest Hero," Trump wrote of Washington. "Without him, our Country and our Freedoms wouldn’t exist."
Trump also criticized the Smithsonian’s recently ended Center for Restorative History, an initiative created to spotlight stories that have been excluded from the national historical narrative.
Trump said the museum should instead create a "Center for American Heroes."

"Tell the stories of Americans who faced great challenges, overcame them, built great things, defended our Country, made America better, and helped our Nation more fully live up to our Founding Ideals," he wrote.
SUPREME COURT CHIEF JUSTICE PRAISES OUTGOING SMITHSONIAN LEADER WHO WAS UNDER PRESSURE FROM TRUMP ADMIN
Those criticisms have also led to action by the White House.
In March 2025, Trump signed an executive order aimed at eliminating what the White House called "divisive narratives" and "improper ideology" at the Smithsonian.
The White House followed this year with a report criticizing the Smithsonian, including what it said was a lack of attention to Washington and other Founding Fathers.
The Smithsonian National Museum of American History in Washington, D.C., Oct. 12, 2025. (Stefani Reynolds/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
In July, Trump ordered his administration to place signs outside the National Museum of American History telling visitors that some exhibits are inaccurate.
In a statement last year, the Smithsonian’s Board of Regents said it was committed to keeping the institution nonpartisan and its scholarship free from political or partisan influence.
The board also acknowledged that the Smithsonian "can and must do more" and directed its leadership to ensure museum content is unbiased.

Smithsonian Secretary Lonnie Bunch announced last week that he will step down at the end of the year.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: GOP women sound alarm as Lindsay Clancy backlash revives calls to repeal 19th Amendment: ‘Definitely a threat’
summary: Republican women warn that online calls to repeal the 19th Amendment after the Lindsay Clancy trial could alienate female voters from the GOP.
story: Republican women Mehek Cooke and Tiffany Losee react to how online calls to repeal the 19th Amendment impact the GOP after Lindsay Clancy's high-profile case sparked online debate over women's voting rights.
If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please contact the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline at 1-800-273-TALK (8255).
Calls to repeal women’s rights to vote are emerging from the online firestorm over the Lindsay Clancy trial, prompting Republican women to warn that the intraparty rhetoric could hurt the GOP.
"I think there’s definitely a threat in the Republican Party right now," political and legal strategist Mehek Cooke told Fox News Digital.

The online calls to repeal the 19th Amendment come after Clancy’s high-profile murder trial ended in a mistrial, with 11 of the 12 jurors favoring a verdict of not guilty by reason of insanity. Clancy admitted to killing her three children, but her defense argued she was not criminally responsible because she was suffering from postpartum psychosis.
LINDSAY CLANCY MISTRIAL DECLARED AFTER JURY DEADLOCKS IN KILLINGS OF HER THREE CHILDREN
Lindsay Clancy listens to testimony Aug. 10, 2026. (Greg Derr/Pool/The Patriot Ledger)
"Convict Clancy. Also Repeal the 19th Amendment!" one user posted on X.

"The female jurors in the Lindsay Clancy trial are speaking out about their deliberations and disagreements with the sole male holdout. The more they speak the better they make the case for repealing the 19th Amendment," another user posted.
Cooke warned that calls to strip women of the right to vote, largely coming from accounts identifying as conservative, risk alienating female voters from the Republican Party.
"When you have these fringe activists online talking about repealing the 19th Amendment or alienating women, it really doesn’t help," Cooke said.

The calls followed after the case made waves on social media, particularly after hundreds of mostly female Clancy supporters gathered outside a Massachusetts courthouse during the murder trial. The demonstrators rallying behind Clancy argued the case is an example of the lack of understanding of postpartum depression.
ROGAN SHREDS SUPPORTERS OF LINDSAY CLANCY, SAYS THEY WOULDN'T RALLY IF A FATHER WERE ON TRIAL FOR SAME CRIME
Supporters of Lindsay Clancy gather outside of Plymouth Superior Court Aug. 20, 2026. (John Tlumacki/The Boston Globe via Getty Images)
But the demonstrations quickly turned into ammunition for online critics who argued that the support for Clancy is an indication that women should be stripped of their right to vote.

"This Lindsay Clancy trial has shown us How spiteful women can be, the fact that women are willing to even defend a child killer just because they want to be ok with the "sisterhood" should alarm you," another user wrote on X.
"They will gaslight you, they will use sign language against you and even try to call you all sort of names. But guess what, they are still wrong and they know it. Repeal the 19th."
Cooke pushed back on the idea that the calls to repeal the 19th Amendment reflect the reality of the mainstream Republican Party.
"Social media isn’t real life," Cooke said. "I think a lot of people out there put these arbitrary crazy ideas, but it doesn’t really reflect what normal people think and what mainstream thinks.
LINDSAY CLANCY MURDER TRIAL BECOMES SOCIAL MEDIA OBSESSION AS TIKTOKERS, SLEUTHS DEBATE CONTROVERSIAL CASE
A protester holds a "Repeal the 19th" sign amid an online debate over women’s voting rights following the Lindsay Clancy trial. (Joseph Prezioso/AFP via Getty Images)

"I think you're getting these calls because of where our culture is today. You looked at the Lindsay Clancy trial and all the women out there in pink that were continuing to support a woman who murdered three children. You're constantly seeing this cultural push in terms of where women stand today in politics."
Tiffany Losee, director of fundraising for The Conservative Caucus, told Fox News Digital that Democrats are to blame for pushing out this agenda and associating it with the broader Republican Party.
"You have to understand this is all a game to the Democrat Party," Losee said. "They’re going to push out anything that looks fringe on the right."

Losee also claimed that Democrats are using this rhetoric on the right to distract voters from the rise of socialism that has emerged within the Democratic Party, claiming if voters understood the ideals of the party, they would "run faster than imaginable to get away from such government control."
HOW THE 'LONG MARCH' THROUGH THE INSTITUTIONS LED TO SOCIALIST TAKEOVER OF DEM PARTY: 'NEED TO WAKE UP'

"They're gonna push out crazy Lindsay Clancy ideas or ‘look over here at something shiny, or communism is cool, socialism is cool, everything's free,'" Losee said. "But then they will not take that extra step to educate the voter on what exactly they are pushing."

Cooke and Losee spoke to Fox News Digital on the issue as Republicans gathered in Dallas for the party’s first-ever midterm convention, where the GOP gathered to rally its base to vote as Republicans work to stay in control of Congress as November’s midterm elections approach.
