title: California football coach arrested after students make disturbing discovery at school
summary: The Tracy Unified School District placed the educator and football coach, Jeffrey Pribble, on leave as separate criminal and district investigations continue.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
A high school football coach in California was arrested Friday after students discovered a cellphone secretly recording them while they were changing inside a campus locker room, police said.
The phone allegedly belonged to Jeffrey Pribble, a 48-year-old teacher at Tracy High School, located east of San Francisco, the Tracy Police Department said Saturday.
According to the school's website and social media accounts, Pribble is the varsity football head coach and works in the school's physical education program.
Pribble has held the coaching position for five years and has 22 years of experience as an educator with the district, according to his Facebook page.
SCHOOL EMPLOYEE ACCUSED OF SECRETLY FILMING 12 GIRLS IN CHANGING ROOM FACES NEW CHARGES
FILE — People walk into Tracy High School in Tracy, California, where football coach Jeffrey Pribble was arrested Friday. (Google Maps)
The discovery was made Thursday when a student and several classmates found the phone recording inside the locker room, officials said.
The students stopped the recording, deleted the video and turned the device over to a teacher.
By Thursday evening, a concerned parent then contacted Tracy police patrol officers, prompting school resource officers and detectives to open an investigation.
The following day, officers determined that the phone belonged to Pribble, who was arrested Friday.
The Tracy Unified School District placed Pribble on leave pending the outcome of separate criminal and district investigations, officials said.
According to the Pleasanton Weekly, Tracy High Principal Jon Waggle acknowledged the arrest of an employee in an email to parents.
FLORIDA MIDDLE SCHOOL TEACHER ADMITS TO YEARS OF 'INAPPROPRIATE' CONVERSATIONS WITH FORMER STUDENT: DEPUTIES
FILE — Jeffrey Pribble served as Tracy High School’s varsity football coach for five years and worked in the district for 22 years, according to his Facebook page. (Google Maps)
The school did not identify the teacher or the specific allegations but noted that the district was fully cooperating with police.

"We understand that this news may raise serious concerns in the District community. The District too is concerned about the well-being of its students and staff and is committed to holding its employees to the highest professional and ethical standards," Waggle wrote.

"Tracy High School and all our Tracy Unified schools are proud of being safe schools. The cooperation between students, parents and staff members keeps our schools safe and is important and appreciated. Thank you for your continued partnership and support."
Tracy Police Chief Sekou Millington added that the safety and privacy of the city's students remain among the department's top priorities.
"Our children deserve to feel safe at school and in every space where they should be able to learn, grow, and simply be kids," Millington said.
FILE — The Tracy Unified School District said Pribble will remain on leave while authorities continue investigating. (iStock)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"Protecting the safety, privacy, and well-being of our students is a responsibility we take seriously. We are grateful to the students who brought this incident to the attention of adults and to the officers and detectives who acted quickly to investigate."
Fox News Digital reached out to Tracy High School for more information.
Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

title: Maryland dad blamed 'Satan' after 2-month-old daughter died from horrific head trauma
summary: A Maryland father blamed "Satan" for his 2-month-old daughter's fatal head trauma that led to her death, as he and the child's mother are facing child abuse charges.
story: Meliza Campos-Sanchez is facing two counts of child neglect, one count of child abuse and an arson charge stemming from an Aug. 16 incident, authorities said. (WSVN)

A Maryland couple was arrested after the death of their 2-month-old daughter who suffered head injuries, with the father allegedly telling police the girl's injuries were caused by "Satan slamming a door on the child," according to charging documents and prosecutors.

Oscar Pineda and Katerin Monzon-Alvarado, both 21, are facing charges for first- and second-degree child abuse, first- and second-degree assault and reckless endangerment that carry a maximum possible sentence of 55 years in prison in connection with the death of 2-month-old Aida Mikea Monzon Alvarado, Baltimore Police said, adding that they could face additional homicide charges pending the outcome of the autopsy report.

The baby was taken to Harbor Hospital on Wednesday with what doctors described as "suspicious" severe bruising around her eyes and jawline. A later examination revealed what charging documents describe as "significant head and brain trauma" and "multiple skull fractures" that were not noticed during the initial examination, charging documents state, according to CBS Baltimore.
IDAHO MOM WHO CLAIMED VACCINES KILLED HER TWIN BABIES CHARGED WITH MURDERING HER KIDS
Oscar Pineda and Katerin Monzon-Alvarado, both 21, are facing charges for first- and second-degree child abuse, first- and second-degree assault and reckless endangerment. (Baltimore Police)

The girl's father allegedly claimed to police that his daughter was injured "due to a supernatural force or Satan slamming a door on the child." The mother said her 2-year-old son often jumps on the bed, which caused the baby to fall onto the floor, a prosecutor said at a court hearing on Friday, according to the outlet.
The prosecutor argued that the extent of the girl's injuries could not have been caused by a single fall from the bed.

Police said the girl's mother brought the baby to the hospital on Wednesday after she became unresponsive. The woman initially told police the baby became unresponsive while lying face down in their bed after she was fed.
ALABAMA MOM CHARGED WITH MURDER AFTER TODDLER BOUND, LEFT TO SUFFOCATE FOR 12 HOURS: COPS
The baby was taken to Harbor Hospital with what doctors described as "suspicious" severe bruising around her eyes and jawline. (Baltimore Police)
Prosecutors said the mother told investigators the child was "freezing and in shock" when she took her to the hospital.
Doctors said the baby "suffered from significant head and brain trauma" and "sustained frontal lobe hemorrhaging and a subdural hemorrhage," according to the charging documents.
Hospital staff could not revive the child, and she died in the hospital.
The girl's father allegedly told police that his daughter was injured "due to a supernatural force or Satan slamming a door on the child." (Tribune News Service via Getty)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Both parents later admitted to investigators that they noticed the girl's bruises on Sept. 6 and that she began vomiting the following day. They said they did not seek medical treatment until she was unresponsive on Wednesday.
The pair is Guatemalan nationals, and prosecutors argued they pose "an extreme flight risk."
Both parents were held without bail.

title: Creepy 'Cat in the Hat' trend targets schools as costumed figure allegedly chases teen girl
summary: A person dressed as the Cat in the Hat allegedly chased a teen girl in British Columbia as the creepy trend sparks school threats nationwide.
story: Citrus County Sheriff David Vincent warns families about disturbing social media posts targeting students, schools and communities. Credit: Citrus County Sheriff's Office

A shadowy figure dressed as the Cat in the Hat allegedly chased a teenage girl through a Canadian neighborhood, as a creepy online trend featuring sinister depictions of the beloved children’s character has prompted investigations and school warnings targeting schools and students across multiple states.

The unidentified girl was walking in West Kelowna, British Columbia, at about 9 p.m. Aug. 24 when a person wearing a costume resembling the Dr. Seuss character allegedly began chasing her, according to the Royal Canadian Mounted Police.
The teen escaped and reached her home safely, but police are still working to identify the costumed individual.
POLICE IDENTIFY SUSPECT ACCUSED OF TERRORIZING PHILADELPHIA WOMEN WHILE WEARING CREEPY CHUCKY-STYLE MASK
A grainy nighttime image shows an unidentified person wearing a Cat in the Hat-style costume as authorities investigate the disturbing trend. (West Kelowna RCMP)
"Regardless of whether the individual intended the behavior as a joke, following a young person and causing them to fear for their safety is extremely concerning," Cpl. Devon Gerrits said.
"People should understand that behavior intended as a prank can have serious consequences when it causes another person to reasonably fear for their safety."
TIMELINE REVEALS HOW MAN IN 'CHUCKY' MASK TERRORIZED PHILADELPHIA STREETS, EVADED POLICE
A phone displays a viral social media video showing a costumed Cat in the Hat figure standing outside a Publix store at night. (Citrus County Sheriff's Office)

Investigators said wearing a costume is not a crime by itself, but pursuing someone in a way that causes reasonable fear could constitute criminal harassment. Assault, threats or intimidation charges could also be considered depending on the evidence.
Anyone who believes they are being followed or pursued should move toward a populated location, contact a trusted adult and call 911 if they are in immediate danger, the West Kelowna RCMP advised.
Police are asking anyone with doorbell, security or dashcam video taken near the 2000 block of Shamrock Drive at about 9 p.m. Aug. 24 to contact the West Kelowna RCMP.

Police have not said whether the real-world chase is connected to a separate "Cat in the Hat" social media trend that has spread across the United States, putting schools on alert and landing some juveniles in custody.
LOUDOUN COUNTY TRANSGENDER SUBSTITUTE CHARGED WITH MAKING SCHOOL THREATS
An edited image places a Cat in the Hat figure outside a small-town theater alongside a message suggesting an extended "visit." (Citrus County Sheriff's Office)

The online trend features edited or AI-generated images and videos depicting a sinister version of the Cat in the Hat lurking outside homes, standing near schools or prowling through communities. Some anonymous accounts have added the names of students, staff members, campuses and towns, sometimes accompanied by ominous messages or threats.
Authorities from California to Florida, Virginia and Texas have responded with investigations and increased patrols as they work to separate internet hoaxes from credible dangers.
TIKTOK IN LEGAL HOT SEAT AS STATE ACCUSES APP OF EXPOSING KIDS TO HARMFUL CONTENT WHILE MISLEADING PARENTS
The Baldwin Park Police Department in California said it was reviewing "concerning social media posts" that referenced local schools and named students and staff members.
"Any threat directed toward our schools, students, staff, or community will not be dismissed as a joke or prank," the department warned.
NEW MEXICO SEEKS MASSIVE PENALTY FROM META AFTER JURY FOUND TECH GIANT LIABLE FOR ENDANGERING CHILDREN
Social media posts show a person in a Cat in the Hat costume referencing George West, Texas. (Citrus County Sheriff's Office)

Police urged residents not to interact with or recirculate the accounts. Anyone who encounters a threatening post is asked to preserve the content, account name, screenshots, dates and times before reporting it to investigators.

In Virginia, the Hanover County Sheriff’s Office launched an investigation after an account posted content referencing Mechanicsville High School and the trend. Deputies increased their presence at the campus while attempting to identify the person behind the account.
UK TO BAN TIKTOK, YOUTUBE, OTHER SOCIAL MEDIA APPS FOR CHILDREN UNDER 16, STARMER SAYS
A social media post shows a Cat in the Hat figure with an ominous message referencing Northampton and the Rushden and Higham area. (Citrus County Sheriff's Office)
The sheriff’s office similarly urged residents not to repost the material, warning that doing so could amplify the message and complicate efforts to trace its origin.

Florida’s St. Johns County Sheriff’s Office said it was investigating content involving county schools but had not identified a credible threat. Deputies nevertheless increased their presence on campuses across the county as a precaution.
Texas law enforcement agencies have also warned that creating or spreading the threatening posts could carry consequences far beyond school discipline.
The Frio County Sheriff’s Office said some anonymous accounts have attached lists of students, schools or communities to menacing images and videos in an apparent attempt to provoke fear.
Authorities there determined posts mentioning the area did not appear to present a credible threat but increased patrols and law enforcement visibility around schools.

"Participating in, re-creating, or spreading these threatening posts is not a harmless joke," the sheriff’s office said, warning that copycat accounts and forwarded threats could lead to charges involving cyberbullying, harassment or terroristic threats.
Laredo police delivered a similar warning, saying criminal charges and arrests may follow even when the person responsible claims the post was only meant as a prank.
GIRL OBSESSED WITH SANDY HOOK, COLUMBINE ALLEGEDLY PLOTTED SCHOOL MASSACRE WITH OTHER STUDENTS: REPORT
A disturbing social media post shows a Cat in the Hat figure beneath a local water tower with the message, "look familiar?" (Citrus County Sheriff's Office)
"A few seconds on social media can result in a police investigation, school disciplinary action, and potentially serious criminal consequences," the department said.

Premont police met with school district leaders after learning of the trend and warned that fake accounts, AI-generated content and purported pranks involving threats could result in charges including making a terroristic threat or filing a false alarm or report under Texas law.
The warnings come as authorities in multiple states have traced threatening accounts to juveniles.

Four girls between 13 and 15 years old were arrested in Berwick, Louisiana, after police linked them to TikTok accounts that alarmed families and schools, according to Police1. Three were charged with terrorizing or menacing, while a fourth was charged with cyberbullying.

A 12-year-old Florida student was accused of posting a written threat to kill tied to the trend, while a 14-year-old Colorado student was arrested after a post referenced a middle school and several homes, the outlet reported. Authorities in Alabama, Ohio and Kentucky have also announced juvenile arrests or pending charges connected to similar posts.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Police across the affected communities have repeatedly asked parents and students not to share the content, even when attempting to warn others. Instead, users should capture screenshots showing the account name and threatening material and send the evidence directly to school officials or law enforcement.
Fox News Digital reached out to TikTok for comment.
Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.

title: Missing 70-year-old hiker rescued after disappearing for a week in remote national park
summary: A Coast Guard helicopter crew hoisted Craig Berg to safety after he went missing for a week while hiking in Michigan’s remote Isle Royale National Park.
story: Craig Berg, 70, was found injured and suffering from hypothermia after disappearing during an extended solo hike. (U.S. Coast Guard Great Lakes)
A 70-year-old man who vanished a week ago while hiking in Isle Royale National Park was found "alive and alert" Saturday, according to officials.
Craig Berg was suffering from hypothermia when he was rescued by Coast Guard and Michigan State Police crews, officials said.
"The Coast Guard and Michigan State Police rescued an injured, ailing man Saturday after he went missing in Isle Royale National Park on Sept. 5," the U.S. Coast Guard Great Lakes said.

Video released by authorities shows a helicopter crew from Coast Guard Air Station Traverse City hoisting Berg from the ground. He was then taken to a regional airport in Gwinn for emergency medical evaluation.
MISSOURI DEPUTY AG, MISSING 6 DAYS AFTER SEEKING TO SUMMIT WYOMING'S TALLEST PEAK, IS FOUND ALIVE
A Coast Guard helicopter crew hoists Craig Berg, 70, from Isle Royale National Park in Lake Superior on Sept. 12, 2026. (USCGGreatLakes; Berg Family via Isle Royale National Park)
Officials did not disclose what happened to Berg while he was missing or provide additional details about his injuries.
Berg was spotted by "good Samaritan" backpackers in the park Saturday before Michigan State Police foot patrols and K-9 units reached him, according to officials.
Multiple agencies and resources were deployed to aid the emergency search, which also included a 45-foot Coast Guard boat, drones and seaplanes.

The search involved the National Park Service, Michigan Department of Natural Resources, Keweenaw County Sheriff’s Office, Wisconsin State Patrol and Minnesota Department of Public Safety, according to Lt. Ben Eckola, a Michigan State Police public information officer.

"We’re also thankful to the fellow hikers who helped, Isle Royale Seaplanes, and No One Left Behind K9 Search and Rescue. Everyone’s efforts played an important part in finding Craig," Eckola said in a statement.
ILLINOIS MAN MISSING MORE THAN A WEEK AS CREWS SCOUR GREAT SMOKY MOUNTAINS NATIONAL PARK
Michigan State Police K-9 officers sit aboard a Coast Guard helicopter over Lake Superior en route to Isle Royale National Park on Sept. 11, 2026. (USCGGreatLakes, courtesy Air Station Traverse City)
The Detroit Free Press reported that Berg, of Royal Oak, Michigan, arrived at the national park on Aug. 27 for an extended solo hike but failed to return home Sept. 5.
Isle Royale National Park is located on a remote island in Lake Superior near the Canadian border.
Due to its remote location, Isle Royale is one of the least-visited national parks and has limited infrastructure.
Berg’s wife, Debbie, told the Detroit Free Press that only two rangers are stationed on the island and that the park has two camp stores and a lodge.
Officials deployed water, land and air crews to search for Craig Berg after he went missing on Sept. 5, 2026. (USCGGreatLakes)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
According to the park’s website, cell phone service is often "unreliable," and many types of equipment are generally prohibited on the island, including bicycles, motorized vehicles and drones.
Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

title: Accused killers vanish after family massacre before manhunt ends hundreds of miles away
summary: A deadly North Carolina shooting left two dead and two critically injured before suspects Camryn Moore and Cory Armstrong fled across state lines.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
A deadly shooting inside a North Carolina family home triggered an urgent search for two accused killers and an interstate manhunt that would end with another burst of gunfire.
Gaston County Police officers responded to a home on Forbes Road at approximately 8:43 a.m. Thursday after receiving a report of gunfire inside the residence.
Officers discovered four people suffering from gunshot wounds. Two were pronounced dead at the scene, while two others were rushed to CaroMont Regional Medical Center with life-threatening injuries.

Police identified the two people killed as Victoria "Heather" Moore, 50, and Megan "Josiah" Bumgardner, 38. The two surviving victims remained in critical but stable condition Friday, according to police.
4 SHOT INSIDE NORTH CAROLINA HOME, 2 KILLED AS POLICE IDENTIFY PERSON OF INTEREST
Gaston County police responded to the Forbes Road home after receiving a report of gunfire inside. (Queen City News)

Detectives identified two residents of the home, Camryn Moore, 26, and Cory Armstrong, 29, as suspects in the bloodshed. WSOC-TV reported that Heather Moore was Camryn Moore’s mother and Bumgardner was her uncle.
Cory Armstrong, 29, was wanted on murder and attempted murder charges following a shooting at a Gaston County home. (Gaston County Police)
Police said they believed everyone involved knew one another and described the shooting as an isolated incident with no continuing threat to the Gaston County community.
Camryn Moore, 26, was accused of killing two people and critically wounding two others inside a North Carolina home. (Gaston County Police)
Investigators have not disclosed what may have triggered the violence.

Camryn Moore and Armstrong allegedly fled Gaston County immediately after the shooting. By Thursday afternoon, detectives had obtained warrants charging each of them with two counts of first-degree murder and two counts of attempted first-degree murder.
WATCH: DEPUTIES HUNT WANTED MAN THROUGH CORNFIELD AFTER HIGH-SPEED CHASE CAUGHT ON CAMERA
Gaston County Police identified two suspects after four people were found shot inside a family home. (Queen City News)

The Gaston County Police Department enlisted the help of the U.S. Marshals Service Carolinas Regional Fugitive Task Force as investigators tracked the pair’s movements across multiple states overnight.
SUSPECTED HUMAN SMUGGLERS LEAD COPS ON 100-MPH CHASE BEFORE BAILING AND ALLEGEDLY COMMITTING ARMED CARJACKING
The search reached Ohio at approximately 8 a.m. Friday, when state troopers spotted the suspects’ vehicle outside Athens and attempted to pull it over, authorities said.

title: Charlie Kirk statue defaced with red paint, Jesus crossed out days after 1-year mark of assassination
summary: Red paint was smeared across the Charlie Kirk statue at Turning Point USA's Phoenix headquarters, with a Christian tribute defaced days after unveiling.
story: President Donald Trump honors Charlie Kirk during a speech at the RNC midterm convention. 'The Five' co-hosts reflect on Kirk's legacy, his impact through Turning Point USA, and the expansion of the group to more than 3,500 high school clubs one year after his assassination.

Vandals smeared bright red paint across a newly unveiled statue of Charlie Kirk and defaced a Christian tribute outside Turning Point USA’s Phoenix headquarters early Sunday, just three days after the memorial was installed.
Images from the headquarters show red paint streaked across the eight-foot statue’s face and neck, with a crude frowning face drawn across its chest.

A sign at the base of the statue bearing Kirk’s image and the words "Jesus defeated death so you can live" was also targeted. The word "Jesus" and an image of a cross appeared to be crossed out, while "Satan" was apparently scrawled across the display.
REMEMBERING CHARLIE KIRK: TURNING POINT USA'S ANDREW KOLVET REFLECTS ON CONSERVATIVE GROUP'S CHALLENGING YEAR
Kirk's widow, Erika, who now serves as Turning Point USA CEO, responded with a defiant vow to rebuild, saying the vandals would not erase her husband’s legacy or silence Christians.
"Charlie once said we should be building two statues for every statue that they tear down," Erika Kirk wrote, adding that her husband’s instinct was always to create rather than destroy.

She said the bullet that killed her husband only amplified his voice and predicted the spray paint would spread his legacy even further. She also vowed to restore the statue, replace Jesus Christ’s name on the damaged sign and continue the movement her husband built.
"God will not be mocked," Erika Kirk wrote.
Phoenix police confirmed to Fox News Digital that the department began receiving calls around 8:09 a.m. reporting vandalism to a memorial in the area of 4900 East Beverly Road.
"Officers have responded to the location, and the incident is under investigation," police said.
No arrests or suspect descriptions had been announced as of Sunday afternoon.

"This morning we woke up to radical criminals vandalizing our headquarters," Turning Point USA Chief Operating Officer Tyler Bowyer wrote on social media. "Crossing over Charlie’s face, scratching out Jesus and the Cross and spraying red paint on his neck.
"This isn’t the country we want to live in," Bowyer added. "Arizona is not Gotham."
INSIDE CHARLIE KIRK’S EFFORT TO DEVELOP THE NEXT GENERATION OF CONSERVATIVE VOICES
Bowyer, who went to the headquarters as police investigated, said TPUSA was prepared to clean the memorial as soon as authorities released the scene.
"God bless the police as they investigate the violent thugs who did this," Bowyer wrote.
TPUSA also released video showing the damage and encouraged its supporters to vote ahead of the midterm elections.
"Hate cannot win," the organization wrote. "The radical Left is showing up to vote. What are you doing to save the country from this?"
In a follow-up statement, TPUSA said it would restore the statue and replace the damaged signs while reviewing footage of the incident and working with law enforcement to identify those responsible.
"Vandalism like this is not funny, it’s diabolical," the organization wrote. "The incident happened in the middle of the night because evil never sleeps."
TPUSA said the vandals went beyond spraying Kirk’s face and neck with red paint, accusing them of making an "intentional decision" to cross out Jesus’ name on the nearby sign.
The organization ended its response by quoting John 15:18: "If the world hates you, keep in mind that it hated me first."
Later Sunday, TPUSA spokesman Andrew Kolvet announced that the statue had been restored.
"The team rallied and got the statue back looking good as new," Kolvet wrote. "Evil may never sleep, but neither do we."
"We won’t stop. We will win. They will lose," he added.
The vandalism struck only days after TPUSA unveiled the bronze statue Thursday to mark one year since Kirk was assassinated while speaking at Utah Valley University on Sept. 10, 2025.
CHARLIE KIRK STATUE BOUND FOR NY'S TIMES SQUARE AS SCULPTOR DEFIES THREATS AHEAD OF UNVEILING
A person visits the makeshift memorial for Charlie Kirk outside the headquarters of Turning Point USA on September 18, 2025, in Phoenix, Arizona. (Joe Raedle/Getty Images)
The statue depicts Kirk wearing his signature "Freedom" T-shirt and cross necklace. Those who knew him said the sculpture captured details down to his wedding ring, according to FOX 10 Phoenix.

Turning Point USA commissioned Utah artist Quintin McCann to create the memorial after he began working on a portrait of Kirk the evening the conservative activist was killed, according to the outlet.
ITALIAN ARTIST UNVEILS CHARLIE KIRK MEMORIAL STATUE HE PLANS TO FEATURE AT TIMES SQUARE

"Someone’s death, who I’ve never met, has never impacted me so much," McCann told FOX 10. "And I’m sure many people can agree. And I just stayed at work that evening and just started sculpting his portrait."
The statue was initially placed outside TPUSA’s headquarters near 48th Street and Beverly Road but was expected to be moved indoors for security reasons by the end of the week, the outlet reported.
REPUBLICAN CONVENTION ATTENDEES SHARE HEARTFELT TRIBUTES TO LATE CHARLIE KIRK ON ASSASSINATION ANNIVERSARY
Conservative voices erupted over the attack, condemning the vandalism as another assault on Kirk’s family, friends and legacy.
"Truly abhorrent," Rep. Abe Hamadeh, R-Ariz., wrote on X. "The Charlie Kirk statue that was just unveiled at Turning Point’s HQ was vandalized overnight with red paint.

"The young people who work at Turning Point don’t deserve this, Charlie’s family doesn’t deserve this, his friends don’t deserve this," Hamadeh added. "The left is intolerant and militant. Evil exists and must be confronted continuously."
Rep. Andy Biggs, R-Ariz., was equally blunt.
"This is absolute evil," Biggs wrote.
Conservative commentator Benny Johnson accused the vandals of trying to intimidate Kirk’s supporters.
"These people are incapable of building anything, all they know is destruction," Johnson wrote. "Keep these demons out of power."
TPUSA contributor Alex Clark said seeing the damage brought her to tears before issuing a dire warning to conservative voters.
"The left wants to tap dance in your blood and throw confetti at your gravestone," Clark wrote. "Vote red in midterms like your life depends on it because it actually does as a conservative."

Turning Point USA Chief of Staff Mikey McCoy urged conservatives to answer the vandalism with faith, invoking Kirk’s willingness to return to hostile campuses and the biblical examples of Stephen and Christ praying for those who persecuted them.

"Then I can surrender all the anger, and pure disgust that I feel at seeing this to a just and holy God," McCoy wrote, saying he would pray instead for the repentance and salvation of those responsible.
"Lord, help our Country," he added. "Open their eyes. Break their hearts. Save them."

Bowyer also blasted Democratic Arizona Gov. Katie Hobbs, accusing her of failing to pursue bipartisanship after Kirk’s killing and pointing to her veto of legislation that would have named Loop 202 in Kirk’s honor.

Hobbs said in her March veto letter that she condemned political violence but argued highway-naming decisions should remain nonpartisan and be handled by the state board responsible for such designations.

Charlie Kirk speaks at Utah Valley University on Sept. 10, 2025 in Orem, Utah. Kirk, founder of Turning Point USA, was speaking on his American Comeback Tour when he was shot and killed. (Trent Nelson/The Salt Lake Tribune/Getty Images)
Kirk was 31 when he was shot and killed during a TPUSA event at Utah Valley University.
Tyler Robinson, 23, has pleaded not guilty to aggravated murder and other charges in Kirk’s death. Prosecutors are seeking the death penalty.

Erika Kirk took over as CEO of Turning Point USA after her husband’s assassination. The conservative organization he co-founded in 2012 has continued expanding its network of high school and college chapters since his death.

title: Arrest rips apart media narrative on death of Black woman found hanging from Mississippi tree
summary: Jarques Ratliff faces a murder charge in the death of Tasia Fortune, a 29-year-old mother found hanging from a tree behind a Jackson, Mississippi home.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

Mississippi authorities have arrested a 51-year-old man on a murder charge after an official homicide ruling in the death of Tasia Fortune, a 29-year-old Black mother of four found hanging from a tree behind an abandoned home last month.

The arrest follows weeks of intense media attention and widespread online discussion regarding the circumstances surrounding Fortune’s death in a state with a historic legacy of racialized violence. But law enforcement officials confirmed that the suspect taken into custody is Jarques Ratliff, a Black Jackson resident who had a prior personal connection with Fortune.

Jackson Police Chief RaShall Brackney announced during a news conference Saturday that Ratliff was taken into custody without incident while walking along Capitol Street in Jackson, shortly after officers executed search warrants at related properties.
AOC’S ‘MODERN-DAY LYNCHINGS’ CLAIM TORN TO SHREDS ONLINE AS BLACK HANGING CASE FINDINGS TELL A DIFFERENT STORY

Chief Brackney emphasized that while the arrest marks a significant breakthrough, the investigation remains active and additional arrest warrants are expected to be served as detectives follow further leads.

Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., last week warned of "racial terror" and "widespread modern-day lynchings" in the U.S. as she joined dozens of Democrats demanding that the Department of Justice investigate hanging deaths of Black Americans.
Christy Spivey poses with a portrait of her late daughter Tasia Fortune Sept. 8, 2026, in Marion, Ky. (AP Photo/George Walker IV)
Fortune’s body was discovered Aug. 3 in the backyard of a vacant property in the 500 block of Road of Remembrance in Jackson.

Although investigators logged hundreds of hours interviewing nearly 15 individuals and reviewing physical evidence over the past month, formal arrest warrants could not be executed until the Mississippi State Medical Examiner’s Office officially classified Fortune’s death a homicide late Thursday.

Once that classification was handed down, members of the Jackson Police Department's robbery-homicide unit moved swiftly to secure and execute two search warrants alongside the arrest warrant for Ratliff.

Addressing public interest in the case, Chief Brackney acknowledged the heightened scrutiny but stressed that law enforcement remains strictly guided by verifiable physical evidence rather than external speculation. She noted that authorities understood public concern given Mississippi's history but said the department is bound to ensure all public statements are backed by forensic facts.
Tasia Fortune in a portrait displayed Sept. 8, 2026, in Marion, Ky. Inset: Jarques Ratliff, who was arrested in connection to Fortune's death. (AP Photo/George Walker IV; Jackson Police Department)

"We understand that this case has received media attention from across the globe and across the community. We understand the questions and the desire for answers given Mississippi's history," Brackney said.

"We understand this case is being viewed through a broader lens — a global lens — and we do not dismiss those concerns. We are taking them seriously. At the same time, we do have a responsibility to make sure that what we say publicly is supported by our evidence and the facts."

Brackney also directly clarified that law enforcement had never officially designated any persons of interest prior to Ratliff’s arrest, refuting social media reports that a 65-year-old man had previously been identified as a suspect.
Jackson Police Chief RaShall Brackney speaking at a news conference. (Jackson Police Department)
COPS DROP MURDER PROBE AFTER CORONER RULES MAN’S BLOODY STABBING DEATH WAS FREAK ACCIDENT

Fortune's mother, Christy Spivey, said police promptly notified her family of the homicide ruling and Ratliff's arrest on Friday. Spivey expressed gratitude for the police work and reiterated her firm belief that her daughter did not die by suicide, adding that Fortune would never take her own life.
Police say Fortune’s body was discovered Aug. 3 in the backyard of a vacant property in the 500 block of Road of Remembrance in Jackson. (Google Maps)

According to family members and an online obituary published in Kentucky, Fortune grew up in Kentucky, skipped her junior year of high school and was a star cross-country runner guided by strong religious faith before relocating to Jackson a decade ago.
Spivey noted that her daughter had experienced homelessness in recent years but was actively working to launch a cleaning business and stabilize her life prior to her death.

Ratliff is being held at the Hinds County Detention Center on a charge of murder. According to Mississippi State Defender André de Gruy, Ratliff is scheduled to make his initial appearance in Jackson Municipal Court no later than Monday morning, where formal charges will be read and bond conditions set.

Police have not publicly detailed the specific physical evidence linking Ratliff to the scene, nor have they expanded on the exact nature of his personal association with Fortune as investigators prepare for further potential arrests.

title: Georgia killer who murdered two suburban real estate agents faces execution after 23-year wait for justice
summary: Lori Brown's mother recalls the 2003 Powder Springs murders of two real estate agents as Stacey Ian Humphreys' Georgia execution date nears.
story: Internet searches from conman Brian Walshe and voicemails from his mother, Diana, take center stage in a new Fox Nation special on the Ana Walshe murder case.

As the execution date nears for a Georgia man convicted of killing two real estate agents, the mother of one victim is remembering the women who were murdered while simply doing their jobs and the risks that real estate professionals still face.
Barring a last-minute judicial stay or executive clemency, Stacey Ian Humphreys, 53, is scheduled for execution Sept. 16 at the Georgia Diagnostic and Classification Prison in Jackson.

On Nov. 3, 2003, Lori Brown, 21, and Cynthia "Cyndi" Williams, 33, were working from a model home office inside the Oakwind subdivision, a rapidly growing, upscale residential development in Powder Springs, when Humphreys fatally shot them.
The office welcomed prospective buyers, making interactions with unfamiliar visitors a routine part of their professions.
74-YEAR-OLD BECOMES FLORIDA'S OLDEST INMATE EXECUTED AFTER 1982 KILLING OF TEEN
Cyndi Williams and Lori Brown (Cobb County Superior Court)
Williams returned to the office after lunch and encountered Humphreys first. Brown arrived shortly afterward and unknowingly walked into an armed robbery already underway.
Humphreys held the women at gunpoint, made them strip and killed them before fleeing with their ATM cards. There was no evidence of sexual assault.

Ed Greathouse, a retired supervisory investigator with the Cobb County Judicial Circuit who assisted the prosecution, told Fox News Digital that investigators never determined why Humphreys chose that particular office over others in the development.
A natural in real estate
For Brown's mother, longtime real estate agent Linda Brown, her daughter’s outgoing personality made her a perfect fit for the profession.
"Let me tell you, she was a rascal growing up," Linda told Fox News Digital. "She had a gregarious spirit about her.
"She was a people person from the time she was small. She never met a stranger. That's why real estate was such a perfect place for her, because she was really good at it."

Brown formed a close friendship with Williams, who took Brown under her wing. She also planned to marry her high school sweetheart in 2004. She had been tasting wedding cakes and looking at venues, Linda said.
On the day she was killed, her wedding planning notebook sat neatly on her office desk.
"Sometimes I think it's my fault. I should have never let her go in this direction with real estate, but, you know, she was going to do what she was going to do," Linda added.
Stacey Humphreys was convicted of murder. (Georgia Department of Corrections)
Arrest and conviction
After the murders, Humphreys used the stolen bank cards to withdraw over $3,000, according to court records.

On Nov. 8, 2003, authorities arrested Humphreys in a rental Jeep Grand Cherokee after a high-speed chase in Wisconsin. Investigators found the murder weapon inside the rental, along with Williams' blood on the gun. They found Brown's blood inside Humphreys’ personal vehicle, according to the Georgia Supreme Court record.
Greathouse said investigators believed Humphreys was heading toward Canada when a Waukesha County officer apprehended him.

"It was fairly common knowledge in prison, where he had been, and certainly in law enforcement, that if you get to Canada, Canada won't extradite you back to the United States unless the prosecutor absolutely will not pursue the death penalty," he said.

Although Humphreys insisted he did not remember killing the women, he told investigators, "I know I did it. I know it just as well as I know my own name."
Authorities learned that Humphreys was behind on his vehicle payments and had taken out a high-interest payday loan he could not afford.

In 2007, a Glynn County jury convicted Humphreys of two counts of malice murder, along with armed robbery, kidnapping and aggravated assault. He pleaded guilty to possession of a firearm by a convicted felon.
THREE DEATH ROW INMATES EXECUTED BY LETHAL INJECTION IN RARE SAME-DAY STRING ACROSS US
Linda Brown remains skeptical that Humphreys' execution will take place after 23 years. (Linda Brown)
In favor of the death penalty
The state scheduled Humphreys' execution for Dec. 17, 2025, but the State Board of Pardons and Paroles postponed the date and his clemency hearing amid legal challenges.
Greathouse said obtaining a death sentence was unusual during his years working capital cases in Cobb County.

"Not only did we lose these two girls, but we had to go through 4½ years waiting for a trial to come to an end. So, here we are 23 years later," she said. "I’m still in favor of the death penalty for this man that took their lives."
Humphreys' attorney filed a motion this past week to try to throw out his death sentence over claims of jury misconduct, but a judge rejected that motion on Thursday, FOX 5 Atlanta reported.

NORTH CAROLINA MAN BROKE INTO EX'S HOME, FATALLY STABBED HIS 5-YEAR-OLD SON BEFORE GOING TO TACO BELL: POLICE

REPEAT OFFENDER RELEASED EARLY FROM JAIL NOW CHARGED WITH CAPITAL MURDER OF PREGNANT WOMAN
Authorities are searching for Kaegan Jude Solet, 47, after identifying him as a person of interest in a series of deadly stabbing incidents. (Terrebonne Parish Sheriff's Office)
The latest investigation is not the first time Solet’s name has surfaced in violent crime allegations.
Solet was arrested in December 2019 after allegedly stabbing a woman repeatedly and leaving her locked inside a Houma motel room, according to a police news release from the time.
Houma police responded to the Red Carpet Inn shortly after midnight on Christmas Eve 2019 and found a 59-year-old woman lying on the floor of her room with numerous stab wounds.

The son of former Somali dictator Mohamed Siad Barre, whose brutal regime was accused of widespread atrocities during his more than two decades in power, has been living in Ohio for years, according to a new report.

Their father ruled Somalia from 1969, until his government was overthrown in 1991. His regime has been accused of mass killings that left as many as 200,000 people dead, torture and other human rights abuses, including atrocities against the Isaaq clan. Mohamed Siad Barre died in 1995.

Historian and Oxford University doctoral researcher Mohamed Haji Ingiriis described Ayanle as his father's "right-hand man" and alleged that he wielded significant power within the government, according to the Post. Fox News Digital has not independently verified those allegations.

An immigration judge determined in 2024 that Ali personally engaged in torture while serving in the Somali National Army and ordered soldiers under his command to detain and torture civilians and assist in extrajudicial killings, according to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).
Ali, who had been living as a permanent resident in Virginia, was deported to Somalia in December 2024.
"The United States will not be a safe haven for those who commit human rights violations," ICE official Russell Hott said at the time.

The Post reported that the company appeared to have operated legitimately and filed the appropriate paperwork.
Some survivors of the Barre regime are now calling for U.S. authorities to investigate members of the former dictator's family.
Human rights activist Suleiman Bolaleh called for an investigation to determine what Barre family members knew or did during the dictatorship, according to the Post.

title: Ex-mayor found liable for alleged sexual assaults of 7 women, ordered to pay $13M
summary: Dominic Foppoli, former Windsor, California, mayor, faces a punitive damages phase after a jury awarded seven women $13 million in sexual assault case.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
The former mayor of a small town in northern California was found civilly liable Friday for allegedly sexually assaulting seven women.
Dominic Foppoli, who led the town of Windsor from late 2018 to 2021, was ordered to pay a combined $13 million in compensatory damages.
The payouts to the women, whose allegations span from 2001 to 2020, will range from $6,000 to $4,650,938 each, KTVU FOX 2 reported.
He could also have to pay punitive damages to the women. That phase of the civil trial will begin on Tuesday.

Foppoli has consistently denied all wrongdoing and has never been criminally charged in connection to the allegations. He stepped down as mayor in May 2021 after four women came forward to the San Francisco Chronicle to accuse him of sexual assault.
FORMER NJ DEM MAYOR ALLEGEDLY DRUGGED, SEXUALLY ASSAULTED CHILD HE MET ONLINE

Dominic Foppoli appears in court during opening statements in the trial held against him at Sonoma County Civil and Family Law Courthouse in Santa Rosa, Calif., on July 15, 2026. (Jessica Christian/San Francisco Chronicle via Getty Images)

The lawsuit, filed in April 2022, detailed allegations from seven Jane Does. Several women alleged Foppoli drugged their drinks before assaulting them, while Jane Doe 1 claimed he raped her dozens of times, including one alleged incident in which she said he handcuffed her to a bed.
According to the San Francisco Chronicle, a total of 13 women have accused Foppoli of sexual assault or misconduct.

In 2024, the state attorney general’s office suspended its criminal investigation into Foppoli, saying prosecutors did not have enough evidence to warrant filing charges on the cases not barred by the statute of limitations at that time.
Foppoli testified during the civil trial, which began in July, again denying the allegations against him.

"I've been a terrible boyfriend and partner, cheating, selfish and egotistical, but I've never done any of those things I'm being sued for," Foppoli said on the stand, according to KGO Eyewitness News.

The jury also found the Santa Rosa chapter of Active 20-30, an all-male charitable social club where Foppoli was a member, liable for Jane Doe 4's alleged assault and awarded her an additional $2 million, the Chronicle reported.

Dominic Foppoli appears in court with his lawyer Andrew Watters at Sonoma County Civil and Family Law Courthouse in Santa Rosa, Calif., on July 15, 2026. (Jessica Christian/San Francisco Chronicle via Getty Images)
FBI AGENTS CONFRONT SWALWELL AT AIRPORT IN NEW FOOTAGE AS VIEWERS ZERO IN AND PILE ON

According to the lawsuit, the woman alleged Foppoli sexually assaulted her during the national Active 20-30 convention in Reno, Nevada, in June 2012. She also accused the organization of failing to investigate complaints she made to its leaders.

Traci Carrillo, an attorney for the plaintiffs, told Fox News Digital that the initial San Francisco Chronicle story "gave some of our clients a voice that no local news agency wanted to touch because it accused a powerful and connected local politician of crimes and sexual misconduct."

"It took over 5 years to get them justice, which was always about accountability. Their trauma was real, and they were believed, not shamed or silenced in the courtroom," Carrillo added. "They feel vindicated and will now focus on the much-needed healing the jury has provided for them."

Foppoli's attorney, Andrew Watters, said in a statement to Fox News Digital that he would seek a mistrial over claims that the court improperly excluded key witnesses for the defense. If that fails, Watters said he would pursue an appeal.

Farrah Abraham arrives for an event at The Sunset Room on June 22, 2019, in Hollywood, California. Abraham accused Dominic Foppoli of raping her in March 2021 at a house party in Palm Beach, Florida. (Gregg DeGuire/Getty Images)

"What happened with the verdict was that the jury sent a message based on questionable self-reported evidence and junk science, and that’s not appropriate. It appears the passions of the jury were inflamed by the evidence, and they hated my client, so they made a very large award to punish and make an example of him," Watters said in a statement.

Foppoli, speaking at a press conference outside the courthouse Friday, said his accusers "are trying to crucify me for a cause I'm not responsible for," adding that they were motivated by the $13 million payout.

Foppoli still faces a separate lawsuit from Farrah Abraham, a social media influencer and former reality television personality who claims the ex-politician raped her in March 2021 at a house party in Florida. That civil case is expected to go to trial next year, according to court records.
The Chronicle reported that Christopher Creek Winery, which Foppoli owns, settled a separate lawsuit filed by a Montana woman who alleged Foppoli raped her multiple times in 2020 when she was 18.

title: Lindsay Clancy DA rarely does plea deals, but her case could be the 'exception,' veteran attorney says

story: Veteran Boston defense attorney Peter Elikann told Fox News Digital the Plymouth County DA is known for rarely cutting plea deals, but Lindsay Clancy's case, after an 11-1 deadlock, could be the "exception."
If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please contact the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline at 1-800-273-TALK (8255).
The Plymouth County district attorney prosecuting Lindsay Clancy is known for rarely cutting deals, but a veteran defense attorney who has worked alongside him says her case may be the "exception."
Clancy, 36, faced three counts of first-degree murder in the deaths of her children — Cora, Dawson and Callan, all under age 6 — who were found strangled at the family's home in January 2023.

Boston-based criminal defense attorney Peter Elikann, who has experience working against the Plymouth County District Attorney's Office, told Fox News Digital that the office is known for its reluctance to negotiate.
SOCIAL MEDIA IS LINDSAY CLANCY WILD CARD THAT COULD TILT POTENTIAL RETRIAL TO THE DEFENSE, RETIRED JUDGE SAYS
Lyndsay Clancy's defense lawyer, Kevin J. Reddington, arrives at Plymouth Superior Court on Sept. 3, 2026. (David McGlynn for Fox News Digital)

Elikann said it has become "conventional wisdom" that it's "unlikely that you'll ever get 12 jurors to agree that she committed first-degree murder."

"A hung jury is not a verdict; jeopardy does not terminate on a hung jury, and a mistrial ordinarily permits retrial," Reddington conceded in the filing.

He argued that 11 of the 12 jurors "applied the reasonable doubt standard," concluding that the prosecutors hadn't proven that Clancy was criminally responsible. The lone holdout on the jury, according to the motion and other jurors, allegedly ignored doubts he had and wanted a guilty verdict.

title: Firefighter caught on camera ripping pro-Palestinian agitator in Elmo costume near Ground Zero on 9/11
summary: Video captured a firefighter confronting a pro-Palestinian agitator in an Elmo costume near the Ground Zero 9/11 memorial service.
story: A firefighter confronts an agitator who was protesting near the 9/11 Memorial on the 25th anniversary of the terror attacks Friday. (X/@FrontlinesTPUSA and X/@choeshow)

A firefighter in New York City called out a pro-Palestinian agitator wearing an Elmo costume with a Palestinian flag as "anti-American" Friday, not far from where the city’s 9/11 memorial ceremony was taking place at Ground Zero, according to video shot by Turning Point USA (TPUSA) and posted to X.
"F------ anti-American motherf-----. Go back to f------ Palestine. We don’t want you here," the man yelled to the protester. It was unclear if he was a current or retired firefighter.
The man told the protester to also take former President Barack Obama, NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani, Gov. Kathy Hochul and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez with them.
MAMDANI DRAWS FURY FROM 9/11 MOURNERS OVER GROUND ZERO APPEARANCE: ‘DISRESPECTFUL’
A firefighter confronts a pro-Palestinian agitator in an Elmo costume Friday. (X/@FrontlinesTPUSA and X/@choeshow)
"Take ‘em all. They’re all no f-----g good!" he yelled. "You’re no f-----g good."
After the firefighter walked away from the agitator, someone yelled in the video, "The Jews are committing a genocide."
It wasn’t clear if it was one of the protesters who yelled it.
"Frustration from Americans attending the 9/11 memorial service a few blocks away is spilling over," TPUSA’s X post said.
HAMAS, HEZBOLLAH FLAGS FLY AT ANTI-ISRAEL PROTEST MINUTES AFTER MAMDANI CONDEMNS TERROR PLOT AGAINST JEWS

title: California woman chased, fatally shot by illegal immigrant DoorDash driver who stalked her for months: DHS
summary: DHS says Shalini Thakur's fatal Sacramento shooting was preventable if Biden administration immigration policies hadn't released her alleged killer.
story: White House border czar Tom Homan slams California sanctuary policies after an illegal migrant is accused of murdering 68-year-old Todd Stewart. Homan discusses the consequences of sanctuary laws and reacts to the Department of Homeland Security introducing new electric-shock gloves to keep federal border agents safe.

The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) said a California woman was fatally shot outside a Sacramento County Panera Bread Tuesday by an illegal immigrant who had stalked her for months and was subject to a restraining order.

Shalini Thakur, 38, was standing near her car when Rohit Rohit, an illegal immigrant from India, approached her, chased her when she tried to flee and shot her in the head before getting in a car and driving away, DHS said.
Responding police officers caught up to him, but Rohit took his own life with a gun, according to authorities.
BIDEN ADMIN RELEASED ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT ACCUSED OF FATALLY STABBING FAIRFAX COUNTY MOTHER

Rohit Rohit, an illegal immigrant from India, stalked a California woman for months before fatally shooting her in a parking lot this week and taking his own life. Rohit entered the United States illegally through Arizona and was released by the Biden administration, the Department of Homeland Security said. (Department of Homeland Security; Getty Images)
"This tragedy would have been completely avoided if it weren’t for the Biden administration RELEASING this killer into our country," a DHS spokesperson said.
"Sanctuary politicians must put an end to reckless policies that play Russian roulette with American lives. Our thoughts and prayers are with the victim and her family."

Rohit spent months stalking Thakur, who was eventually granted a restraining order. Thakur said she knew Rohit as a DoorDash delivery driver who would park outside her home for hours and talk to her on a daily basis, ABC 10 reported.
DEADLY HOSPITAL STABBING PUTS NEWSOM UNDER PRESSURE OVER ICE DETAINER FIGHT
FILE - Officials alleged Rohit was a DoorDash delivery driver. (CFOTO/Future Publishing via Getty Images)
Rohit had stalked Thakur since at least January, when she found an Apple AirTag under the hood of her car.
At one point, he tried to coerce her into marriage and prevented her from socializing with others, the news report said. He also allegedly threatened to shoot himself or anyone she met.

Rohit later deflated her car tires and followed her to work so he could pretend to offer her help, authorities said. At one point, Rohit allegedly obtained a copy of Thakur's apartment key so he could enter her home while she slept.
FILE - DHS said Rohit illegally entered the United States through Arizona in August 2023 and was arrested by U.S. Border Patrol before later being released. (Gregory Bull/Associated Press)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Even after she got a restraining order against Rohit in May, he continued to stalk her as recently as July.
"She could have been saved. She told police so many times," Thakur’s mother, Sudesh Kumari, told the news outlet. "She called them, but nobody did anything."

Rohit illegally entered the United States through Arizona in August 2023 and was arrested by U.S. Border Patrol. He was released as part of the Biden administration's policy to let migrants into the U.S. after they were given a court date to appear before a judge.
DoorDash did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

title: Houthis enter US 'kill box' after seizing Red Sea 'cork,' former Pentagon official warns
summary: Houthi rebels seized Perim Island in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, but a former Pentagon official warns they've entered a vulnerable U.S. Navy kill box.
story: Houthis seize Perim Island, exposing themselves to U.S. firepower, former Pentagon official says.

Iran-backed Houthi rebels captured Perim Island in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait Sept. 11, opening a new front at a vital global shipping chokepoint as a former Pentagon official warned Sunday the militants had entered a "kill box."

The island's capture came after a month-long offensive along Yemen’s western coast that killed more than 1,500 soldiers and forced Yemen’s government to acknowledge a "painful" defeat, according to The Associated Press.
"With Perim, they have gained what we could call the cork in the Red Sea bottle," Morgan Murphy, a former Pentagon press secretary and retired Navy captain, told Fox News Digital.

"But they've put themselves into a kill box. They're nowhere near the capability of the United States and if the president so chooses, he can wipe them off the face of that rock pretty easily," Murphy warned.
SAUDI ARABIA TELLS TRUMP NOW IS THE TIME FOR MILITARY ACTION AS IRAN-BACKED HOUTHIS ADVANCE
The Houthis reached the strategic island of Perim in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait on September 11 in a move to tighten their grip on a vital global shipping route. (Reuters)
Despite Perim sitting in the middle of the narrow maritime passage, Murphy detailed how the Houthis had effectively placed themselves in an area that is vulnerable to concentrated fire.
"Perim cuts that chokepoint right in half, and it's only 18 miles wide there," Murphy said.
He said the island has served as a pivotal maritime vantage point for hundreds of years, previously targeted for control by French forces and held by the British Empire for over a century.

Perim — a desolate volcanic island also known as Mayun — also sits roughly 20 miles off the Horn of Africa, placing it in proximity to Camp Lemonnier in Djibouti, home to one of the largest U.S. military installations on the continent.
"We have incredible firepower in that region, and that's a little rock in the middle of that strait. It's a volcanic rock. It doesn't have any water. It's uninhabitable," Murphy warned.
"There's no vegetation to speak of. And the Houthis have just massed their troops on that rock. So what that is, what we would call that in the Navy, is a kill box."

Satellite imagery of the island shows a 1.85-kilometer (6,070-foot) runway alongside three military hangars, which regional intelligence reports attribute to past construction by the United Arab Emirates.
"There's a 6,000-foot airstrip on that island. I think that Emiratis built it," Murphy said.
‘GATE OF TEARS’ AT RISK: IRAN THREATENS MAJOR NEW GLOBAL CHOKEPOINT IF US MOVES ON HORMUZ

"It's nice to have an airstrip, and especially a long runway, but we don't know the condition of that runway. We don't know how they could possibly use that runway, and they certainly don't have the sophisticated air power that the United States and its allies have to project power from that runway."
He added that the U.S. military holds overwhelming force options if commanders elect to target the island.
"We could wipe that rock into glass, just blast it into a smooth glass surface, put skates back on our feet, and skate all over it," Murphy said.
"That's why the Houthis have kind of played coy with the president, and they know that even if they fortify that rock they're not going to be able to hold it in the face of the United States Navy."
The developments come amid diplomatic maneuvering between Washington, Riyadh and the Houthis in recent days.

Sources confirmed to Fox News Digital that Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman had called President Donald Trump twice Sept. 10 to urge him to authorize U.S. military strikes against Houthi positions.
Trump declined direct intervention, with U.S. officials noting the administration has no immediate plans for direct combat involvement but will continue offering intelligence assistance.
IRAN AND HOUTHI TERROR PROXY FACING RED SEA THREAT FROM PRO-US AFRICAN NATION

Satellite imagery shows Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a key shipping waterway and the gateway to the Red Sea, as Iran threatens using Yemen's Houthi allies to shut the Bab el-Mandeb gateway to the Red Sea, in this handout picture dated July 12, 2026. (Nasa Worldview/Handout via Reuters)
Speaking to reporters in Dublin on Sept. 12, Trump also indicated the Houthis had signaled a desire to avoid direct confrontation with American forces.
"The Houthis called us, and they don’t want to fight with us. They let us know, they don’t want to fight with us... they don’t want us to go after them," Trump said.
Murphy suggested, however, that Washington’s restraint should not be mistaken for inaction.
"I can't speak for the president. But this administration has not shown a lack of resolve to use force," Murphy said.
"I wouldn't doubt at all if the president took steps to pound some of these folks into the sand if they continue to really disrupt the global energy supply."

Yemeni government, regional and Iranian sources told Reuters the Houthi advance was sustained by Iranian weaponry and tactical direction from the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, or IRGC, with U.S. officials estimating hundreds of IRGC officers remain active in Yemen.
Murphy noted that Tehran's strategy appears designed to drive up global fuel prices by choking critical shipping lanes.
TRUMP THREATENS 'MAJOR MILITARY PUNISHMENT' FOR IRAN OVER FUTURE HOUTHI ATTACKS

Protesters who support Yemen's Houthi group brandish weapons and shout slogans as they celebrate the ban imposed against the maritime shipping of Saudi Arabia on July 20, 2026, in Sana'a, Yemen. (Mohammed Hamoud/Getty Images)
Comparing the conflict to historical naval power struggles, Murphy emphasized the strategic mismatch.
"We're in a different era. They are nowhere near the sophistication of the world's major powers. The Houthis are using a 19th-century playbook. They are not using 21st-century warfare," he said.
"So, yes, they've caught a critical cork in the Red Sea bottle, but how they use it remains to be seen," Murphy concluded.

"This is an example of why great powers really have to have a strong Navy. This is why Great Britain had a strong navy. This is why the United States has a strong navy, because there's so many regional powers who want to try to bottle up shipping, whether it is in the Strait of Malacca, whether it is in the Strait of Hormuz, and here, in this case, in the Red Sea."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"I think what we're going to see in the next several days and weeks is a coordinated effort by the Trump administration to make sure our allies are on board in helping us keep these critical waterways open, free, and clear for freedom of navigation," he said.

Emma Bussey is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital. Before joining Fox, she worked at The Telegraph with the U.S. overnight team, across desks including foreign, politics, news, sport and culture.

title: Could Africa be the next AI frontier as US and Europe hit limits?
summary: U.S. companies are winning massive data center and AI deals across Africa, including a $6.2 billion project in Lesotho for hydropower and computing.
story: China expert Gordon Chang discusses why he believes Beijing is looking to exploit U.S. opposition to new data centers as China works to narrow America’s lead in AI infrastructure.
FIRST ON FOX: Africa could become the next major frontier for data centers and artificial intelligence, experts say.
The Trump administration is backing and promoting American companies to make AI development, in their words, "the gold standard."
The U.S. is trying increasingly to grab business opportunities in Africa as backlash and environmental restrictions hit data center development in the U.S. and Africa.

"Africa is emerging as a significant potential location for building AI infrastructure, especially as many mature markets face increasing environmental and power constraints," Abhishek Goyal, consultant at specialist research group Arizton Advisory & Intelligence, told Fox News Digital.
US COMPANIES WIN BILLIONS IN AFRICAN DATA CENTER DEALS IN DIRECT COMPETITION WITH CHINA

A rendering of U.S. company Cybastion’s projected data center in the Ivory Coast, West Africa. The U.S. Embassy in Abidjan helped facilitate a $170 million contract with the government of the Ivory Coast, which includes the provision of the data center.  (Cybastion)

"The continent could become the next major frontier for AI infrastructure development. As the U.S. and Europe encounter challenges such as power scarcity, grid congestion, permitting issues and environmental regulations, Africa's underdeveloped infrastructure presents an opportunity rather than a disadvantage."

A State Department spokesperson told Fox News Digital, "We are committed to ensuring that American AI, including enabling infrastructure like data centers, continues to be the gold standard worldwide and that we remain the partner of choice for foreign governments and businesses who are seeking to upgrade their telecommunications networks and AI capabilities."
Amongst other deals, this year with U.S. help, an American company has won a $6.2 billion deal in Lesotho in Southern Africa for a data center and hydropower plant.

In the central African country of Gabon, the U.S. Embassy helped win $600 million in business for American companies in 2025. And this year, the embassy in this central African country has assisted in securing a $100 million contract to supply two data centers and a gas-to-power plant in the face of strong competition from China.
TRUMP GETS MAJOR WIN AGAINST CHINA IN AFRICAN RARE EARTH MINERALS RACE

A rendering of the Kobong, Lesotho, Pumped Hydro project, which is to be constructed in Lesotho by U.S. company Convalt Energy as part of a $6.2 billion deal with the government of Lesotho facilitated with the assistance of the U.S. government. (Convalt Energy)

Assistant Secretary of State for African Affairs Frank Garcia previously told Fox News Digital, "Under President Trump’s leadership, the United States is assisting U.S. companies to find new markets and flourish in Africa."

"Africa is experiencing a data center boom, but it begins from a very small base," Arthur Goldstuck told Fox News Digital. Goldstuck is CEO of South African technology research group World Wide Worx and author of "The Hitchhiker’s Guide to AI – The African Edge."
MASSIVE AI BOOM PUTS ONE OF AMERICA’S OLDEST MANUFACTURERS ON PATH TO DOUBLE IN SIZE, CEO SAYS

Goldstuck said that because of a lack of capacity, "Africa will not replace either market as any kind of center of global computing. Rather, its attraction lies in serving a rapidly growing African cloud market and processing African data closer to the people and businesses that generate it.

He continued, "Africa also gives U.S. companies access to a cloud and AI market that remains severely underserved. The opportunities extend from operating data centers to supplying AI chips, cooling systems, cybersecurity and power infrastructure.

"In some countries, a data center can also become the guaranteed customer that makes a new renewable energy project financially viable. American companies can therefore develop computing capacity and electricity generation together, in partnership with African companies and governments."

A recent site visit to the construction zone for a new data center in the Ivory Coast, which is part of a $170 million contract facilitated by the U.S. Embassy for development by the U.S. company Cybastion.  (Clement Djakey for Cybastion)
But Goldstuck said data center growth is fueled by local needs on the continent.

"It is a boom by African standards," he said. "Africa remains far behind the U.S. and Europe in installed capacity, and weak electricity grids make construction and operation more difficult. Demand is growing rapidly as governments, banks and other large companies seek local cloud and AI services. They increasingly want sensitive information stored within their own countries, which adds momentum to the expansion."
Arizton’s Goyal added that "countries such as South Africa, Kenya, Nigeria, Morocco and Egypt are attracting large-scale (AI) projects.

"The U.S. government aims to offer credible solutions that leverage public and private financing in priority areas, such as emerging technology, which demand that global telecoms networks remain secure for U.S. citizens and business," a State Department spokesperson said.
"For example, undersea cable networks are being constructed across the Atlantic, providing more opportunity and connectivity to Africa than ever before."
THE BIGGEST THREAT IN AMERICA'S RACE WITH CHINA ISN'T BEIJING, TECH EXECUTIVE WARNS

The Isando Campus, home to the Teraco Data Environments JB1 East & West, JB3 and JB5 data centers, in Johannesburg, South Africa, Sept. 28, 2025. Outside South Africa, computing resources on the continent are often expensive and scarce.  (Leon Sadiki/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
U.S. companies using undersea AI cables to connect with African data centers is a possibility, Goldstuck said, but there are limitations.

"Distance creates a slight delay, so African facilities would be less attractive for U.S. services requiring an instant response from American users" Goldstuck said. "They could work well for backups, disaster recovery and some intensive AI processing, provided that the cost, security and legal jurisdiction made sense."

Analysts say much of Africa lacks regulation and is creating the risk of a Wild West approach to business. The South African government recently claimed the country hosts 70% of the continent's total data center capacity.

But Pitso Tsibolane, senior lecturer in information systems at the University of Cape Town, told Fox News Digital that, in South Africa, "there is currently no public register of data center facilities, no requirement that operators disclose how much water, electricity and land they will use and no binding commitments against which performance can be measured.
The Isando Campus, home to the Teraco Data Environments JB1 East & West, JB3 and JB5 data centers, in Johannesburg, South Africa, Sept. 28, 2025.  ( Leon Sadiki/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
"That gap serves nobody. Communities cannot see what is being traded on their behalf, and responsible operators cannot distinguish themselves from the rest because nobody’s numbers are on the table.

"South Africa hosts the majority of Africa’s data center capacity and has a real opportunity to become the jurisdiction that gets this right early: transparent disclosure, an independent factual baseline and predictable approvals. That combination is good for households, good for the grid and good for every investor who intends to be here for the long term."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Arizton’s Goyal says the future for Africa could be bright.

"Several African countries present a unique opportunity due to their abundant renewable energy potential — such as solar, wind, hydro and geothermal sources — as well as available land, lower development costs and fast-growing digital economies," Goyal said.
Paul Tilsley is a veteran correspondent who has reported from four continents for more than three decades. Based in Johannesburg, South Africa, he can be followed on X @paultilsley.

title: Sweden votes as migration, crime and economy dominate high-stakes election
summary: Gun violence, asylum policy and welfare reform dominate Sweden's election as Ulf Kristersson's coalition battles Magdalena Andersson's Social Democrats.
story: ‘Saturday in America’ host Kayleigh McEnany discusses President Donald Trump’s visit to Ireland, warnings to Europe over its immigration policies and more on ‘Fox & Friends Weekend.’

Swedes head to the polls Sunday with Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson’s center-right party slightly behind the center-left Social Democratic Party led by Sweden's former prime minister, Magdalena Andersson, and the election dominated by fears of mass migration, crime and the economy.

"Years of gang violence, Islamist extremism, persistent unemployment and pressure on public services have intensified the debate over whether integration has kept pace with immigration," foreign policy expert and author Daniel Schatz, told Fox News Digital.

Sweden Democrats party leader Jimmie Åkesson addresses an election campaign event at Sjodalsparken in Huddinge near Stockholm Aug. 18, 2026, as part of his party's national campaign tour ahead of Sweden's upcoming general election in September.  (Jonathan Nackstrand/AFP via GettyImages)
After Germany's AfD victory in a state election last week, Sweden's hard-right Sweden Democrats are in a position to enter government if Kristersson's party wins again.
DENMARK'S LEFT-WING PM WARNS: 'BIG ENEMY HAS STARTED TO GROW FROM WITHIN' AS EUROPE FACES MIGRANT RECKONING

The Associated Press reported that the anti-immigration party has shifted toward the political mainstream and is likely to get cabinet posts. It has so far supported the Kristersson government from the outside.

The Associated Press reported that the Sweden Democrats were founded by activists in far-right-wing extremist groups, including neo-Nazis. But since then, under its leader, Jimmie Åkesson, it toned down that rhetoric and kicked out racist members. Åkesson, who has led them since 2005, is said to be responsible for the success of a once marginal party.
Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson trails in polls as Sweden holds its general election Sept. 13 to elect members of its parliament, the Riksdag. (Kristian Tuxen Ladegaard Berg/NurPhoto)
Sweden, once a model of the Western social welfare state, has been under economic strain as governments from both the left and the right were forced to restructure their welfare system.
While social benefits continue to be extensive, Sweden’s welfare state has changed amid rising crime rates, but the expectations for public benefits remain.

"Sweden went from being described as a ‘humanitarian superpower’ to a 'humanitarian basket case.’ Discontent with migration policies extends to both foreign-born and native-born residents. Shootings have declined sharply, but fewer shootings do not mean the integration problems are solved," Schatz, who is Swedish, added.
Gang violence has rocked parts of Sweden over the last few years. (Oscar Olsson/TT News Agency/AFP via Getty Images)

Prime Minister Kristersson’s government took power in 2022, when the nation was experiencing a dramatic rise in gun-related violence, with the country witnessing 391 shootings resulting in 62 deaths, according to The Swedish National Council for Crime Prevention, a government agency under the Ministry of Justice.
SWEDEN JAMS SUSPECTED RUSSIAN DRONE NEAR FRENCH CARRIER AS NATO WAR FEARS RISE
The homicide rate in Sweden has been on the rise since 2013, when gun homicides contributed to a general increase in Sweden’s total homicide rate.
The Swedish National Council for Crime Prevention notes that Sweden’s homicide rate ranks high compared with other European countries, at approximately four deaths per million inhabitants per year.
The average for Europe is approximately 1.6 deaths per million inhabitants.
Swedes go to the polls on Sunday in a closely watched election race. (Fredrik Sandberg/TT News Agency/AFP via Getty Images/Sweden OUT)

The issue of immigration is another major issue that dovetails with voters’ concerns over crime and gun violence. Like much of Europe, Sweden experienced a wave of immigration in 2015 coming from those fleeing the Syrian civil war as well as the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan.
Sweden took in over 160,000 asylum seekers in 2015, or 12% of all those who sought protection in the EU, according to Sweden’s Migration Agency.

"After the 2015 influx of asylum seekers from Syria and other war-torn countries strained its reception system, Sweden began tightening its borders. The current government has taken that shift much further," Schatz said.
ANTI-MIGRANT AFD SEEKS TO BREAK GERMANY’S POLITICAL ‘FIREWALL’ IN HISTORIC STATE ELECTION

Election campaign posters featuring Swedish Prime Minister and Moderate Party leader Ulf Kristersson are displayed in central Stockholm, Sweden, on Sept. 7, 2026. (Jonathan Nackstrand/AFP via Getty Images)
Prime Minister Kristersson’s parliamentary ally, the right-wing Sweden Democrats, filled the void in the anti-immigration position in parliament.

Nicholas Aylott, professor of political science at Södertörn University in Stockholm, told Fox News Digital the link between the increase in immigration and the rise in crime changed Swedish politics.
Magdalena Andersson of the Social Democrats leads the polls against the incumbent Prime Minister, Ulf Kristersson. (Anders Wiklund/various sources/AFP via Getty Images/Sweden OUT)
"Migration and law and order became much higher electoral priorities," Aylott said.

"The Sweden Democrats based their pitch on them. The other parties, rather belatedly, adapted their positions. The Sweden Democrats had at first been completely ostracized by the other parties, but they were gradually accepted as a legitimate partner by three of the other parties of the right between 2018 and 2022," he said.
As anti-immigration backlash rose and the Sweden Democrats were more included in the policymaking process, Sweden cracked down on immigration and made it harder to seek asylum.

While asylum claims dropped and gun violence was dramatically reduced as well, with only 158 shootings and 44 fatalities to date, the government still might suffer a defeat at the hands of Andersson’s center-left coalition.
