Living in America
Adults living in the South (17.7%) and Midwest (17.5%) were more likely to experience frequent fatigue than adults living in the West (15.6%) or Northeast (14.5%), the report showed.
The CDC survey didn’t look at underlying causes of frequent fatigue, and it doesn’t indicate whether it’s worse than in previous years.
Add to Google
Add to Google
But Dr. Alana A. Lewis, a cardiologist at the Bluhm Cardiovascular Institute at Northwestern Medicine in Chicago, said the findings were “not unexpected.”
“Just living in this country, we all, at some point, feel fatigue,” Lewis said.

In the most recent “Stress in America” survey, the American Psychological Association found that a majority of adults reported feeling isolated, left out and more stressed about the future than they used to be.

Stress can cause surges in hormones like cortisol and adrenaline, which can wear a body down. That increasing stress contributes to an uptick in fatigue, said Jennifer Caspari, a clinical psychologist licensed in Denver and Vancouver, British Columbia.
“People are incredibly busy,” Caspari said. “They’re stressed. They’re feeling spread thin. They have a lot on their plates and only so many hours in the day. They’re trying to cram in so much.”
Stress can also lead to mental health issues like anxiety and depression, which can disrupt sleep, causing us to feel more tired throughout the day, Caspari said.
Women report more fatigue
More than half of women said they felt fatigue “some days,” and 20% experienced it “most days or every day.”

Caspari said chronic health issues, like autoimmune diseases, which often include fatigue as a symptom, affect women in greater numbers. Hormonal fluctuations during menstruation, pregnancy, perimenopause and menopause can also affect energy levels.

And many women in heterosexual relationships, for example, say they feel they have more responsibilities at work and home than their male partners do, which can lead to them feeling exhausted, Caspari said.
Even when tasks are evenly divided, women experience stress differently. They tend to worry more about organizing and planning and engage in more “internal dialogue” about their responsibilities.
How to deal with fatigue

Mental health, lifestyle and physical health are the “three big pillars” that can trigger fatigue, Lewis said. Heart disease, obstructive sleep apnea, anemia and thyroid issues can also be underlying causes of fatigue.
When patients complain of fatigue, Lewis asks:
Are you getting enough sleep? Are you eating well? Are you exercising?Are you on your screen all day?
Are you getting enough sleep?
Are you eating well?
Are you exercising?
Are you on your screen all day?
“Start with the basics,” said Lewis, who encourages patients to follow the American Heart Association’s Life’s Essential 8 cardiovascular health checklist.
Pay attention to your sleep and stress patterns to determine whether fatigue is a temporary issue or something that’s become more “chronic and persistent,” which could indicate a medical problem.
Learning to relax, both physically and mentally, is important, said Caspari. Take a break from never-ending to-do lists. “You’re not a robot. You only have so much energy,” Caspari said.
Passive resting, like sitting down to watch TV, is perfectly fine. Caspari also recommends “active rest,” low-intensity activities like breathing exercises and gentle stretching.
“Active rest can feel more nourishing,” she said, “and it can have a more helpful impact on the fatigue over time rather than just sitting and scrolling.”

title: Your health insurance bills are about to go up
summary: Most Americans can expect to pay significantly more each month for health insurance next year, whether they get it through work, the Affordable Care Act or Medicare.
story: Most Americans can expect to pay significantly more each month for health insurance next year, whether they get it through work, the Affordable Care Act or Medicare. In some cases, the premium increases may be the largest in decades and are driven by numerous economic pressures. But they won’t look the same for everyone. Some will pay more in the form of higher copays or deductibles.

“Healthcare costs are going up faster than they have in years, and open enrollment is when the healthcare affordability crisis is really going to hit home for people,” said Larry Levitt, executive vice president for health policy at KFF, a nonpartisan research group. “That’s true for whatever kind of insurance you have.”
Prices have shifted upward in every corner of daily life.

The rising healthcare costs stem in part from higher prices for hospital and other medical care, as well as the increased use of expensive prescription drugs — including GLP-1 weight loss medications — that are driving up spending for insurers and employers.
The pressures are unique to each type of coverage.

People who buy insurance through the Affordable Care Act marketplace, about 19 million adults, are set to face another year of steep premium increases after the enhanced federal subsidies expired last year.

On Thursday, the White House promised $500 rebate checks to an estimated 1 million ACA enrollees, alleging they were wrongly overcharged. It’s unclear where the money for the rebates would come from or whether the distribution would require approval from Congress, but experts say it’s unlikely to provide significant relief.

The $500 check “pales in comparison to the increased premiums that marketplace enrollees are facing due to the expiration of the enhanced subsidies,” said Miranda Yaver, an assistant professor of health policy and management at the University of Pittsburgh.

Workers with job-based insurance may be asked to shoulder more of their employers’ rising health costs. And some Medicare beneficiaries could see changes to their prescription drug premiums after the Trump administration ended a temporary program that helped keep those premiums in check.
Here’s what to expect.
The Affordable Care Act
People who buy health insurance through the ACA are on track for a second straight year of double-digit premium increases.

Insurers who offer ACA plans are proposing a premium increase of about 15%, on average, for 2027, according to a KFF analysis of public filings from insurers across all 50 states and Washington, D.C. For 2026, insurers upped rates by an average of 20%.

People earning $80,000 a year who don’t qualify for standard ACA subsidies could see the cost of their bronze plans — the cheapest plan — rise by roughly $80 a month, adding almost $1,000 to their annual tab.

One of the biggest reasons insurers are hiking rates is that medical care is getting more expensive, Levitt said. Insurers have pointed to higher prices for hospital stays, doctor’s visits and prescription drugs, among other costs.
Insurers generally “have felt pressure to add coverage of GLP-1 drugs for weight loss, but they’re also seeing big, big increases in costs for those drugs,” Levitt said.

The ACA marketplace is also still adjusting to the expiration of the enhanced federal subsidies at the end of 2025. Those subsidies — first put in place during the pandemic — lowered monthly premiums for millions of people in the middle class. When they expired, people either paid significantly more for coverage in 2026 or downgraded their plans.
The expired subsidies also led ACA enrollment to fall by about 3 million.

Young adults — who are generally healthier and more likely to go without insurance when it becomes too expensive — accounted for a large portion of the enrollment decrease. That left insurers with a group of customers who, on average, need more medical care, Yaver said, which was also factored into insurers’ rates for 2027.
Job-based health insurance
Most Americans, about 165 million people, get health insurance through their jobs. Many of them may be feeling the price increases, too.

Employers expect the cost of providing health benefits to each worker to rise 8.2%, on average, in 2027 — the largest increase since 2003, according to a survey of more than 1,800 employers by Marsh, a benefits consulting group.

That doesn’t necessarily mean workers’ premiums will rise by 8.2%, said Dr. Kevin Schulman, a professor of medicine at the Stanford University School of Medicine who researches employer-based health insurance.

Employers typically subsidize a large portion of workers’ health coverage. But when healthcare costs rise too sharply, Schulman said, employers have several ways of passing some of the increase along to employees. They can charge workers more for their monthly premiums, raise deductibles or make other changes to their benefits.
Sometimes, they slow wage increases to offset the expense.

“Because the costs are going up, the employers are trying to reduce the rate of growth, and the easiest way to reduce the rate of growth of healthcare costs is to push more of the costs onto the employee,” Schulman said.
Many appear prepared to do just that.
The Marsh survey found about two-thirds of large employers — those with 500 or more employees — said they expected to increase how much employees contribute toward their premiums in 2027.

Others may shift costs in other ways, including waiving copays and deductibles for primary care visits while charging for other kinds of care, or keeping premiums the same while raising the deductible.

For workers, that makes it important to look beyond the premium during open enrollment, Schulman said. A plan that costs less or about the same each paycheck may come with a higher deductible or require people to pay more when they seek care.
Medicare
Monthly premiums are handled somewhat differently for the roughly 70 million people enrolled in Medicare.

People on Medicare generally have more than one premium to consider: typically, a premium for Part B, which covers doctor’s visits and other outpatient care; and, for 9 out of 10 enrollees, a separate premium for Part D, which covers prescription drugs.
Prescription drug costs are where enrollees may see the biggest changes, according to Yaver, of the University of Pittsburgh.
The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services projected in July that the baseline monthly cost for Part D coverage will rise about 6% in 2027, from $38.99 to $41.33.
What enrollees actually end up paying varies, depending on their income and their specific plan.

The increase stems from the Trump administration withdrawing its support for a temporary federal program that helped offset premium increases for Part D plans. The program began in 2025 as Medicare’s prescription drug benefit underwent major changes under the Inflation Reduction Act. Without it, enrollees would have seen their monthly premiums nearly double, according to a report from the Government Accountability Office.
The change will hurt seniors, Yaver said, noting that the program had reduced the average premium by 40% last year. People on Medicare are often retired and live on fixed incomes.
“Though seniors don’t change their Part D plans often, this year may be an exception, potentially resulting in seniors opting into lower-quality plans, leaving them less protected,” she said.
Enrollees will still have an annual out-of-pocket cap on prescription drugs. In 2027, the cap is $2,400.

title: Texas Republicans call out railroad commissioner candidate over racist post
summary: Several prominent Texas Republicans on Sunday condemned a racist post by Bo French, a GOP candidate for statewide office to regulate Texas’ oil and gas industry.
story: Several prominent Texas Republicans on Sunday condemned a racist post by Bo French, a GOP candidate for statewide office to regulate Texas’ oil and gas industry.

French, who is running for state railroad commissioner, posted a photo of students of South Asian descent at the University of Texas celebrating the school’s football win over Ohio State on Saturday, saying, “The problem is now obviously far worse than anyone imagined.”

French was quickly met with backlash from his own party, as Sen. John Cornyn, who is leaving Congress after he lost in a primary to Trump-backed state Attorney General Ken Paxton, condemned the post and urged fellow Republicans to do the same.

“This is the Republican nominee for statewide office. Are other Republican elected officials going to condemn the intolerance and racism, or look the other way while it becomes normalized. This is how great political parties self-destruct. Sad,” Cornyn wrote on X.
French responded by calling Cornyn a “RINO” and saying Texas institutions were “overrun by illegal aliens and foreign nationals.”
“He and the other America Last losers are mad that Texas Republicans are starting to put America First,” French wrote.

Rep. Dan Crenshaw, R-Texas, condemned French on X as well, while Democratic state Rep. Jon Rosenthal, who is running against French for railroad commissioner, said French could not “tell a Longhorn from a foreigner.”
Gov. Greg Abbott did not condemn the post in a statement Sunday, but he said that French’s message was not his and that the photo he posted was “selective” and “shows a way that Texans unite.”

“The way we win the state is the same way we win football games. We unite under the brand of Texas,” Abbott said. “That doesn’t mean that Texas cannot also lead in having the toughest immigration laws of any state in America and freezing H-1B visas at our universities.”
French in May defeated the Abbott-endorsed incumbent, Jim Wright, for the GOP nomination for railroad commissioner.

Texas House Speaker Dustin Burrows called on French to delete the post, writing: “You can oppose immigration policy without demeaning people because of their race or ethnicity — this post has crossed the line.”

The Democratic nominee for the Senate, James Talarico, lauded Cornyn for his statement, while condemning French’s post and questioning his opponent, Paxton, about whether he, too, would speak out against it.
“Racism has no place in Texas,” Talarico wrote.
Paxton responded to Talarico’s post by saying he condemned “racism in all its forms” — without making mention of French or French’s post and while attacking Talarico.
French has a history of making bigoted remarks. He has used slurs against the LGBTQ community and has made antisemitic and Islamophobic remarks.

French did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Asked by WFAA-TV of Dallas in July whether he regretted those comments, French said he did not, adding, “Truth sounds like hate to those who hate the truth.”
The Texas Railroad Commission is a powerful three-member panel that regulates oil and gas production, pipelines and natural gas utilities in the state. Members serve six-year terms.
A spokesperson for the University of Texas did not immediately respond to a request for comment Sunday about French’s post.

title: Mariska Hargitay and Peter Hermann’s Love Story, In Their Own Words
summary: Mariska Hargitay and Peter Hermann met on the set of “Law & Order: SVU” and have been married for 22 years. Ahead of the Emmys, here’s what to know about their relationship.
story: Mariska Hargitay and Peter Hermann first met on the set of “Law & Order: Special Victims Unit.” Now, 22 years of marriage later, they are going as strong as ever.

Hargitay has had a big year. Her directorial debut, the documentary “My Mom Jayne” is up for an Emmy Award and she’s set to make her hosting debut as emcee of the Sept. 14 ceremony. She also made her Broadway debut in “Every Brilliant Thing.” Her final show on July 5 was a true family affair, with Hermann appearing on stage to propose to his wife’s character.
Hargitay and Hermann started dating shortly after their initial encounter in the early 2000s, and in 2004, they got married. They’ve since welcomed three kids: August, Amaya and Andrew.
In a March 2018 interview with People, Hargitay opened up about the life that she’s created with Hermann.
“My husband is my North Star, and my kids are my teachers,” she said.
“Our family is so perfect, or at least perfect for me,” Hargitay added. “Together we’re just this whole, happy, joyful, chaotic, crazy unit. I’ve never known anything that was more right.”
Here’s a timeline of Hargitay and Hermann’s relationship, and what they have said about each other and their family in interviews.
They Met on ‘Law & Order: SVU’ in 2001

Hargitay and Hermann met in November 2001, per InStyle, when he guest-starred on Season 3 of “Law & Order: SVU.” Hargitay plays Olivia Benson, now captain of the Manhattan Special Victims Unit, and Hermann played defense attorney Trevor Langan. Since then, he’s appeared in other episodes of the 27-season show.
During a January 2022 appearance on “The Drew Barrymore Show,” Hargitay recalled their first encounter and said that she was “nervous” to be around him because he was so “handsome.”
“It was distracting,” she said.
Hargitay noted that her first thought after meeting Hermann was, “Who is that Clark Gable Superman guy that I need to marry today?”

Hargitay laughed about how her friends kept telling her that she should put herself out there more because no one was just going to show up on “Law & Order: SVU” and marry her. To their surprise, and to hers, that’s exactly what happened.
Their First Date Was at Church
Months after meeting on “Law & Order: SVU,” Hargitay said that she and Hermann were having a discussion about religion, per InStyle. She said Hermann then asked her to go to church.
Faith is important to both Hargitay and Hermann.
“I think God is very much in us. Faith is a huge part of our life. And I think everything happens for a reason,” Hargitay told SF Gate.
During the sermon, Hargitay told TODAY she got emotional — not because of the church environment, but because of their connection.

“I cried because I was feeling something that I’d never felt before, but I kind of knew what it was and I always say people, well, you know, when you’re a little girl, your parents and your grandparents and everyone goes, ‘When you’re in love, you’ll know.’ And I did,” she said. “And before I did I’d never felt that. And so when I was sitting in church, it was so hilarious, because Peter was like, ‘Oh my God, she’s so moved.’”
They Got Married in 2004
In August 2004, Hargitay and Hermann got married in Santa Barbara, California, in front of 200 guests, per People.

“I think we both knew, sort of, what we found,” Hargitay later told People in 2019. “We sort of knew that we found the right one. I never thought it could be this good, and I never knew that I’d be reminded on the journey, that I’d marry the right one. That I waited and married the right one and it’s better than I thought it was. Because sometimes you take a snapshot and you go, ‘I can’t believe this is my life.’”
They Welcomed Son August in 2006
In June 2006, Hargitay and Hermann welcomed their first child, son August Miklos Friedrich Hermann.

“Nobody wanted to be pregnant more than me,” the “Lake Placid” star told SELF magazine in 2007. “From the minute I found out, I was wearing full-on maternity pants. My stomach was totally flat, mind you, but I was just so excited.”
In a 2019 interview with Traveling Mom, Hargitay said having a child made her and Hermann more “compassionate toward other people.”

“You go from being that person who would get annoyed at the sound of a crying baby, hoping it would just go to sleep, to the one who is completely empathic toward the parents, hoping the baby is OK and wondering if there is anything you can do to help,” she said. “Now, we’re all in the same boat. We’re on the same team, which is one of my favorite things about becoming a parent. I feel like I’m in the club now.”
They Adopted Daughter Amaya in April 2011
In April 2011, Hargitay and her hubby adopted daughter Amaya Josephine Hermann.

“I’m deliriously happy,” Hargitay told People at the time. “From the minute she was born, she was just surprisingly alert and so full of love.” According to People, the couple’s daughter was born in the United States.
Before Hermann and Hargitay adopted her, they were “considering both international and domestic adoption” for their second kid.
“We talked a lot about mixed-race adoptions, and we are very excited that we are now a multi-racial family. We’re just so happy she’s here,” Hargitay said.
As for August? The “Tales from Earthsea” star noted that the then 4-year-old took to being an older brother easily.
“He calls her his baby because he says the whole thing was his idea,” she said. “He always talks about how he’s going to protect her. He’s going to be a great big brother.”
... And They Adopted Son Andrew Months Later
In October 2011, Hargitay and Hermann adopted their third child, son Andrew Nicolas Hargitay Hermann, just months after they became parents to Amaya.
In an interview with People, Hargitay said that she barely had any clothes to give him because she gave all of August’s old clothes to her godson, who was born a few months before Andrew.
“It was so hilarious,” she said.
But thanks to her friends, Hargitay was able to clothe her baby in a few onesies that they brought over.

While Hargitay and Hermann were considering adopting another child, Andrew’s adoption came more quickly than anticipated. In an interview with Good Housekeeping, Hargitay explained they received word of a premature child and that saying yes was a “no-brainer.”
“It was like … a miracle. And I don’t use that word lightly. I’ve never made a bigger decision so quickly,” Hargitay aid.
Once the paperwork was finalized, Hargitay told People they felt “so lucky” to be parents again.

“We never in a million years thought it would happen this quickly, but something inside of us knew that this was right, and we said, ‘Yes, yes, yes!’” she explained to People. “We knew this was our guy. Everything about it felt right. It felt divinely right.”
After taking Andrew home, Hargitay felt more joy than she could ever imagine.
“I always describe it as this angel that fell out of the sky, because he was a little unexpected,” she told People in 2019.

“It’s something that happened very quickly, when adoption can take a long time,” Hargitay added. “We were so beautifully and surprisingly … not because we’re not in sync, but surprisingly in sync about something so huge. So momentous.”
They Just Celebrated Their 22nd Anniversary
In August 2026, Hargitay and Hermann celebrated their 22-year wedding anniversary.
To commemorate the occasion, Hargitay shared a black-and-white photo of them in Cannes, France, seemingly from 2025, when she debuted “My Mom Jayne” at the city’s film festival.
“Happy 22nd anniversary Peter Hermann. You’ve got all my love,” she captioned the photo.
Mariska Hargitay Revealed How She Keeps Her Marriage So ‘New and Fresh’

Amid their 20th wedding anniversary, when asked how she keeps their marriage so “fresh,” Hargitay told Jenna Bush Hager on TODAY with Hoda & Jenna that it has everything to do with how she views their romance.

“I’m at a point in my life where it just keeps getting better with him. And marriage is not always like this,” Hargitay said, while putting her arm in an upright position, “or any relationship that is deep in matters. But, I have learned so much.”

“Peter always says this beautiful quote about ... breaking through marriage into marriage,” she continued. “And that is what I think we’ve lived because at this time in my life, I feel very different than I have for the last maybe 15 or 18 — and I feel (assured) up in our love.”
Mariska Hargitay and Peter Hermann Have Brought Their Kids to Red Carpets

While rare, Hargitay and Hermann occasionally bring their three kids to red carpets, including in May 2023, when the whole family attended the Stuttering Association for the Young Benefit Gala in New York City.
Hargitay and Hermann have been outspoken about August, now 20, and his stutter. Both actors were inducted into the Stuttering Association for the Young’s Hall of Fame.
“It’s been so exciting to learn and to understand and educate people because as soon as people know, they’re like, ‘Oh, my gosh. Thank you. Tell me more. Tell me more,’” Hargitay told People in 2023.
In 2025, Hargitay brought August, Amaya and Andrew along for several red carpet events for her film “My Mom Jayne,” including its debut at Cannes Film Festival and its New York City premiere.
Peter Hermann Proposes To Mariska Hargitay (For A Second Time)

At Hargitay’s closing night performance of “Every Brilliant Thing,”  an interactive one-person play and Hargitay’s Broadway debut, Hermann filled an audience-participant role given to someone in the crowd.
The role of Sam, the character’s childhood best friend and eventual spouse, was played by Hermann during Hargitay’s July 5 show.
Hermann got down on one knee to act out a proposal, which received lots of laughter and cheers from the audience.
Hargitay and Hermann shared an on-stage hug and a kiss to close out her Broadway run.
Peter Hermann Plays Plus One At Creative Arts Emmys Awards
Mariska Hargitay took home two trophies at the Creative Arts Emmys Awards on Sept. 5.
Peter Hermann, adorned in an all-black suit, walked the red carpet with Hargitay following the ceremony, and the two posed together with her hardware.

For her documentary “My Mom Jayne,” Hargitay won outstanding documentary or nonfiction special. From her role as director, she also secured the win for outstanding directing for a documentary/nonfiction program.

title: Our 1 Big Question for Mariska Hargitay During Commercial: How Does It Feel to Be Mariska Hargitay?
summary: Mariska Hargitay opens up about the healing she found in making “My Mom Jayne,” hosting the Emmys and how Knicks point guard, Jalen Brunson, has inspired her.
story: When the camera cuts, the interview isn’t over. With “Cut for Time,” TODAY.com asks the questions our anchors couldn’t get to on air.

In Hollywood, there are A-listers and then there’s royalty. Mariska Hargitay lands in the latter category. The daughter of screen legend Jayne Mansfield, Hargitay has followed in her mother’s footsteps, becoming luminary in her own right for her portrayal of Olivia Benson on “Law & Order: SVU.”
It’s a role that’s earned her both an Emmy and a Golden Globe. Not to mention that, at 27 years and counting, it’s the longest-running primetime series in NBC history.

On this day, however, Hargitay hasn’t come to unpack the latest season of the crime drama. Instead, we sit down in TODAY’s Orange Room to talk about the latest season of her life, a chapter that’s been especially fulfilling for a number of reasons.

Among them? She’s just wrapped her successful Broadway debut, sat courtside with bestie Taylor Swift before her beloved Knicks took home the championship, and premiered the deeply personal film “My Mom Jayne,” which earned the 62-year-old yet another an Emmy nomination.

If she wins, she won’t have far to go to pick up the trophy since Hargitay is also hosting the Emmys this year, the first time a woman has hosted the awards show since Jane Lynch held the distinction back in 2011.

It’s undoubtedly Hargitay’s moment. The actor reflects on the “profound healing” that got her here and how the Knicks’ Jalen Brunson played a part in it. She also delves into her work with the Purple Leash Project, a partnership between Purina and the nonprofit RedRover that spotlights the need for more pet-friendly domestic violence shelters, an initiative near and dear to her heart.
This interview has been lighted edited for clarity.
First of all, I just want to acknowledge the fact that I didn’t think about it either and that’s what hit me so hard when I learned about it, because I don’t think anybody thinks about that.

So, it’s a really powerful and extraordinary initiative. Just the idea that a survivor shouldn’t have to choose between her safety and her animals. There’s already so many barriers of why not to leave and why not to go, but this one is a huge one.

This idea that pets are actually family members and oftentimes the most consistent, steady presence in a survivor’s life, that provides so much comfort, so much support, so much safety, really. And here was a reason that people weren’t going.

Up to 50% of survivors were not wanting to go, to leave their animals. So, it’s actually a brilliant initiative to a way of  supporting survivors. It takes that off their plate and they’re doing it all over and I was just so moved by it and so happy to get on board.

They’re like your children. They are an extended part of your family. Also, the idea of animals being used as threats or used as tactics to keep the person there or threaten that if they leave, they’ll hurt the animal. More than 70% of women in shelters report that their abuser has used an animal as a form of control.
So, it’s innovative, brilliant and so survivor-centric. And it is truly something that supports healing and gives survivors the courage to leave and supports them in a profound way.

I’ll tell you what it feels like: When I made this film, everything changed. I think the way I described it is finding so much more internal space that I didn’t have. It really settled my nervous system and was very profoundly healing for me in ways I was aware of, and in ways that I wasn’t.

My friend Kelli Giddish, my amazing co-star, had said to me after she saw (“My Mom Jayne”), because she knows me very well, she says, “I can’t wait to see what you do next,” and that really resonated with me really deeply.
For me, it wasn’t an accident that all this ... it was like a pathway started opening up because I think, and I’ve always believed, that the only way out is through. That’s sort of my motto.
This is also why I made this film, this is why I did that. Because I was carrying something that I didn’t want to carry and I realized, wasn’t mine to carry.

So, in a way, yes, I’m doing all these amazing things and I’m doing all these new things. In a way, it’s surprising and sort of unbelievable. And in a way, it feels like, “Of course. Now.” Because I’ve gotten ready for it internally.

I’ve always been a person to take on new challenges, but the fact that these opportunities are coming – I think that something shifted. So when the play came, I was 62. My mother was 22 (when she made her Broadway debut), and I made this film. So, I just believed that it wasn’t an accident that after I made the film, it sort of cleared that out and dealt with it and had a new reconciliation and new peace with it and so much new discovery.
So, the fact that the play came, I went, “Of course it did.” And I feel a little bit like that with the Emmys. As much as it was a shocker for me, I went, “Got it.”

Even Jalen (Brunson), all the Knicks stuff, that’s been so fun and exciting and he really is like my excellence mentor or my teacher of what’s possible in a very similar way that my dad was for me. I think that’s what also I love about him because my dad said, “You can do anything, you just have to set your mind to it.” That’s how I was raised.

So, when I see what Jalen has accomplished with the odds he goes up against, and his work ethic, and the fact that he holds a space to win, always, always, there’s no quitting ever with him, which is what my dad taught me.

It’s like, we don’t quit in this family. We keep going. It depends how much you want it. So it’s sort of this beautiful duality, that on one hand it’s, “Oh my gosh.” And on the other hand, it feels natural and I’m excited and ready in a way.

title: How to Watch the 2026 Emmys Red Carpet Ahead of the Ceremony
summary: Stars from some of the biggest shows of the past year are in Los Angeles to celebrate the 2026 Emmys.
story: Stars from some of the biggest shows of the past year are in Los Angeles to celebrate the 2026 Emmys.

The 78th Emmy Awards, hosted by Mariska Hargitay, will air live on NBC and stream on Peacock on Monday, Sept. 14. The Television Academy announced the star-studded list of nominees in July, and many of them are expected to make appearances.

Actors like Jason Bateman and Oscar Isaac are battling in the stacked outstanding lead actor in an anthology series or movie category, which includes Riz Ahmed, Charlie Hunnam and Matthew Rhys, too. Meanwhile, Zendaya is trying to pick up her third Emmy win in the outstanding lead actress in a drama series category for her portrayal of Rue in “Euphoria.” But, she faces tough competition from fellow nominees Carrie Coon, Keri Russell, Rhea Seehorn and Chase Infiniti.
While television fans are waiting to find out who will snag the trophy, they are also looking forward to seeing what the actors will be wearing when they make their grand arrivals at Peacock Theater.

And it’s not just the nominees who will be dressed to the nines. Previously announced presenters like Sarah Michelle Gellar, Keke Palmer, Florence Pugh, Marcello Hernández and more will be in attendance as well to hand out awards throughout the night.
Make sure you don’t miss a moment of the show, including the arrivals during the pre-shows. Find out how to watch all the red carpet arrivals below.
When Are the 2026 Emmys?
The 78th Emmy Awards will be broadcast live from coast—to—coast on NBC on Monday, Sept. 14. The show will also be available to stream live and on demand on Peacock.
The ceremony begins at 5 p.m. PT/ 8 p.m. ET.
How to Watch the 2026 Emmys Pre-Shows
There will be plenty of pre-shows that fans can tune into to catch all the major moments from television’s biggest night.

E! will air its “Live From E!: Countdown to The Emmys” special starting at 2 p.m. PT/ 5 p.m. ET. The pre-show will last for one hour and will be hosted by Erin Lim Rhodes, along with Lance Bass and Ciara Miller.
Then, Justin Sylvester, Keltie Knight and Will Marfuggi will step in to lead “Live From E!: 2026 Emmys” for two hours before the show begins, starting at 3 p.m. PT/ 6 p.m. ET.

Those who prefer streaming to cable can check out People and Entertainment Weekly’s websites. Throughout the day, both outlets will be posting red carpet interviews on their sites and respective social media platforms.
NBC will also be active on social media, with a pre-show TikTok live from the red carpet. The livestream will kick off at 4:45 p.m. PT/ 6:35 p.m. ET on tiktok.com/@nbc.

Another pre-show option for Los Angeles locals is KTLA’s “Live From The Emmys” rundown. Newscasters Jessica Holmes and Melvin Robert will share details with viewers live from the red carpet from 3 p.m to 5 p.m. PT. Journalist Megan Henderson and Doug Kolk will also be on hand to report.

Finally, CNN and Variety are teaming up to bring fans joint coverage. “CNN & Variety: Red Carpet Live: TV’s Biggest Night” will be available on CNN’s website and on the CNN app for subscribers at 2 p.m. PT/ 5 p.m. ET. CNN reporter Elizabeth Wagmeister and Variety’s co-president and co-editor-in-chief Ramin Setoodeh will work together for the coverage.
How to Watch the 2026 Emmys Backstage Feed
Once the show officially begins, Emmys.com and youtube.com/@televisionacad will stream footage live from a backstage feed.

The behind-the-scenes videos will include moments from the Thank You Cam, Backstage Cam, Emmy Photo Lounge and Winnerviews, which will be hosted by Albert Lawrence. Fans can also check out additional clips from the red carpet, show and press room.

title: From ‘Traitors’ to ‘Dancing With the Stars,’ Mark Ballas Had to Learn to Trust Partner Maura Higgins
summary: Mark Ballas shares with TODAY.com his experience competing on “Traitors” with his now-“Dancing With the Stars” partner Maura Higgins.
story: Mark Ballas’ main goal when competing on “Dancing With The Stars” is always for his celebrity partner to “enjoy the experience and try our best.”
But when he found out that for Season 35, he would be partnered with his former “The Traitors” co-star Maura Higgins, he had to adjust a bit and learn how to trust her.

“‘The Traitors’ is a wild psychological experience,” the 40-year-old professional dancer and three-time Mirrorball champion tells TODAY.com. “And we made it to the last episode together. She made it further than me, obviously, to the last two (people). I think I made it to the last six or last five.”

Season 35 of “DWTS” will kick off with a two-night premiere on Sept. 15 and Sept. 16. During the first episode, only the male celebrities will perform, while Ballas and Higgins will get to show off their skills on the second night when only the female celebrities get to compete.
Previously, the two appeared on the fourth season of “Traitors,” the hit Peacock competition series, which is famously known for its backstabbing and deceitful game play among contestants.

While the pair were both “Faithfuls,” contestants spend the duration of the season, unsure of whether they can trust their fellow players who may just be “Traitors” in disguise who will “murder” — aka eliminate — them.

“We got along, but at the same time we couldn’t fully trust each other because, I mean, there was a moment where I was convinced it was her and Rob (Rausch),” Ballas says, referencing his fellow competitors. “So much stuff didn’t make the edit on ‘The Traitors.’ (We had) so many conversations. However, we did have a laugh together ... But you can’t trust each other in there. You’d be stupid to.”

The two, however, did bond during their time on “Traitors,” dishing on their European ties. Higgins is Irish and Ballas grew up in England with a Texan father and a British mother, both of whom were ballroom dancers.
He recalls Higgins, who also starred in “Love Island UK,” telling him while in the Scottish castle that she would love to compete on “Dancing With the Stars.”

“I was like, “Girl, you can’t make it through a 45-minute challenge. You ain’t making it through ‘Dancing With the Stars,’” he jokes. “But she was like, ‘No, it’s different. I want to dance. I want to learn how to dance. I don’t want to carry gold pebbles in a backpack up a mountain.’”
After their “Traitors” experience, they saw each other at the reunion. Higgins also attended his “Chicago The Musical” show on Broadway.
But when he found out she was his partner, he thought, “‘This is hilarious,’ because she manifested this, right? I’m a big believer in manifestation.”
While Higgins has never had any dance training, he says “she’s a hard worker.”

“To my surprise, after seeing her in the challenges on ‘The Traitors,’ I’ve been impressed with how she’s putting a chin down and getting into it,” he says. “But she is a true beginner, which is exciting. I’m excited about that challenge. And we have to also establish real trust and friendship because in ‘The Traitors,’ unless you play that game, I can’t explain what it does to you mentally. It’s wild.”
For their competition debut, the pair will perform a foxtrot to “Black Velvet” by Alannah Myles. In preparation, Ballas has been making sure the reality star is diving into the experience.
Ballas’ No. 1 tip for aspiring dancers, regardless of experience? Don’t hold back.
“Take the dive off the diving board. Don’t be afraid,” he says. “If you’re signing up for something like this, really make sure you want to do it. And if you’re here, try your best.”

He hopes all his partners have felt like they’ve gotten the best experience they possibly could have with no regrets. As for Higgins, he calls her a “great personality” and has helped her loosen up by having her poke fun at him.

“I’m a very full-out, expressive person as it is. So when we’re learning moves, I’ll demonstrate a move and I’ll do it almost over the top, silly,” he shares. Then he will ask his partner to re-create the move “and nine times out of 10 when they do that, they nail it.”
In Higgins’ case, he says, “I was like, ‘Can you just make fun of me for a minute?’ And she made fun of me, did the face and threw her arms and I was like, ‘Yes, like that!’”
For now, he stresses that this is a once in a lifetime experience for the celebrities, encouraging them to really take it in.

“Think about it, it’s quite silly. Like, we’re ballroom dancing on telly and you get a new style every six days, and you’re just hoping that you make it to the end,” he says. “For me the mission is, every week just a bit better, as long as we last.”

title: Celebrities Turned The U.S. Open Into A Masterclass On Style
summary: The tournament, which concluded on Sept. 13 with Alexander Zverev besting Ben Shelton in the men’s singles finals, also featured some impressive style from celebrities.
story: Fans may have attended the U.S. Open for the exceptional tennis, but they got a serving of great style on the side.

The tournament, which concluded on Sept. 13 with Alexander Zverev besting Ben Shelton in the men’s singles finals, has become one of the biggest events in sports, boasting star-studded crowds and a whole lot of excitement at the Arthur Ashe Stadium in Queens, New York. And celebrities have matched the energy with some truly exquisite looks.
From star athletes to actors, check out the many celebrities who brought some striking looks to one of the most buzzy sporting events of the year.
Paris Hilton

If there’s one thing reality star Paris Hilton is going to do, it’s stun. Hilton hit the Blue Carpet in pieces from Thom Browne and Gucci. She paired her sweater top and skirt with an adorable pink dog purse for the occasion.
Eiza González
Actor Eiza González went for a chic monochrome off-white look with a high-neck, sleeveless bodysuit and trousers.
Maitreyi Ramakrishnan
Actor Maitreyi Ramakrishnan hit the Blue Carpet with a flowing, patterned summer dress and open-toed black heels.
Spike Lee and Tonya Lewis
In true Spike Lee fashion, the director attended the tournament, repping the New York Yankees. His wife Tonya Lewis Lee sported a classic brown suit, paired with pointed-toe heels.
Alysa Liu
Figure Skater and Olympian Alysa Liu pulled up to the U.S. Open in her signature tomboy style with a camo-colored jacket and pants, paired with a plain white tee.
Pink and Jameson Moon Hart

Singer Pink coordinated her U.S. Open look with her son, Jameson Moon. The singer wore a green jacket with a white shirt-and-pants combo underneath, while Jameson rocked a green-and-white striped fit.
Jordyn Woods
Model Jordan Woods went with a denim ensemble, completing the look with a chic brown bag and, of course. The newlywed also flashed her gorgeous emerald-cut diamond ring.
Trinity Rodman

Soccer star Trinity Rodman, whose boyfriend Ben Shelton is playing in the men’s singles finals, brought many standout looks to the Open. But one highlight was this plaid zip-up jacket and skirt combo, completed with a bright orange cap.
Morena Baccarin and Ben McKenzie
Actor Morena Baccarin hit the Blue Carpet with an orange leather dress while her hubby and fellow actor Ben McKenzie wore a classic button-down and maroon trousers.
Ashlyn Harris and Sophia Bush

Former pro soccer player and two-time World Cup champ Ashlyn Harris wore a long-sleeved white button down and pin-striped trousers to the Open. Meanwhile, her girlfriend actor Sophia Bush  sported a green jacket, paired with a white dress and shoes that flaunted mis-matched colors.
Daniela Rajic and Paul George

Boston Celtics’ Paul George dressed up a Brown Ralph Lauren shirt with a flashy cross necklace. His wife and entrepreneur Daniela Rajic went for a black halter top and white pants, paired with a black mini-purse.
Savannah Guthrie and Michael Feldman

TODAY’s Savannah Guthrie hit the Blue Carpet, wearing a long floral, striped skirt, a plain black top and a heart-shaped necklace. Her husband Michael Feldman sported a classic blue suit and dressy sneakers.
Olivia Palermo
Influencer and fashionista Olivia Palermo rolled up to the U.S. Open in a polka-dotted dress paired with pink flats that had red accents on top.
Natalia Bryant
Model Natalia Bryant, daughter of the late basketball great Kobe Bryant, attended the tournament wearing an off-the-shoulder button down dress. She opted to pair the outfit with a pair of flip-flops.
Trae Young
Washington Wizards’ Trae Young went for a sporty look, with an off-white button down shirt to match his shorts.
Landry Shamet and Cameron Aimonetti

New York Knicks’ Landry Shamet brought some color to the Blue Carpet with a patterned sweater and burgundy hat. His camera strapped around his neck added an extra touch. His fiance Cameron Aimonetti sported a classic white button-down and jeans.
Aziz Ansari
While comedian Aziz Ansari kept his look classic with a striped blue button-down and khaki pants, he added just a bit of spark with a pair of oversized shades.
Ali Marks and Jalen Brunson

New York Knicks captain Jalen Brunson arrived at the U.S. Open, wearing a khaki jacket paired with a plain white tee. His wife, Ali Marks, sported a floral sleeveless dress and a red sweater, wrapped around her shoulders.
Tommy Hilfiger and Dee Ocleppo Hilfiger

Designers Tommy Hilfiger and Dee Ocleppo Hilfiger showed up to the match sporting the classic Hilfiger red, white and blue colors. Dee Ocleppo Hilfiger wore a plaid jacket while Tommy Hilfiger opted for a classic suit and sweater.

title: Hayden Panettiere’s Ex Brian Hickerson And His Brother Involved In A Bar Altercation, Police Say
summary: Brian Hickerson, Hayden Panettiere’s on-again-off-again boyfriend, was recently involved in an altercation at a bar in South Carolina, police say.
story: Brian Hickerson, Hayden Panettiere’s on-again-off-again boyfriend, was recently involved in an altercation at a bar in South Carolina, police say.

The Greenville Police Department identified Brian Hickerson and his brother Zachary Hickerson as two individuals involved in the incident at Wild Wing Cafe on Sept. 12, law enforcement told NBC News in a statement.
Zachary Hickerson, who was “highly intoxicated,” was taken into custody and charged with disorderly conduct while Brian Hickerson was released from the scene, police said.
The incident comes just weeks after a police report showed that the brothers were present when Panettiere was pronounced dead on Aug. 18.
Zachary Hickerson and Brian Hickerson did not immediately respond to NBC News’ requests for comment.

According to Greenville Police, officers were dispatched to the restaurant at around 9:10 p.m. on Saturday in response to a reported assault. The officers detained multiple patrons as the situation was being investigated before determining that Zachary Hickerson had been heavily inebriated.

“He began yelling profanities in a public setting, and as a result, he was taken into custody for disorderly conduct and transported to the Greenville County Detention Center,” police said in a statement.
Brian Hickerson was not charged.

In August, EMS personnel responded to a 911 call to Panettiere unresponsive at an apartment, where the brothers also were, according to a heavily redacted police report. Panettiere was in cardiac arrest when emergency personnel arrived. A cause of death has not been released.

Zach Hickerson was “very emotional” during the resuscitative efforts on Panettiere, Greenville Officer Matthew Bryan wrote in the report. Brian Hickerson “did not become emotional until EMS declared her officially deceased,” Bryan wrote.

title: When Are the Emmys? How to Watch 2026 Awards Show
summary: The 78th Emmy Awards will see some of the biggest Hollywood stars going head to head in the major categories.
story: The 78th Emmy Awards will see some of the biggest Hollywood stars going head to head in the major categories.

The 2026 Emmy Awards, television’s biggest night, will be held on Monday, Sept. 14, in Los Angeles. The ceremony will be broadcast live from Peacock Theater and feature nominees like Zendaya, Oscar Isaac, Steve Carell, Colman Domingo and more.

Mariska Hargitay, who’s cemented her icon status for her portrayal of the beloved “Law & Order: Special Victims Unit” protagonist Olivia Benson, will be hosting the ceremony.  It marks the first time a woman has hosted the awards show since Jane Lynch in 2011.
Hargitay herself has already won two Creative Arts Emmys on Sept. 5 for her deeply-personal film “My Mom Jayne,” about her mother, screen legend Jayne Mansfield.
Nominations were first revealed on July 8, with TODAY exclusively sharing the nominees for outstanding variety series and outstanding reality competition program.

After all the categories were announced, “The Pitt” led with a staggering 25 nominations. “Hacks” closely followed with 24 nods for its fifth and final season, which set a record in the comedy category. Rounding out the top three was new series “Widow’s Bay” with 19 nominations.
There were also 28 actors who received their first-ever Emmy nominations. Some of them have already added “Emmy winner” to their resume, after taking home an award at the Creative Arts Emmys.
Soon, more stars will be presented with the coveted golden statue.
Read on to learn everything you need to know about the 2026 Emmys.
When Are the 2026 Emmys?
The 2026 Emmys are set to air live on Monday, Sept. 14, beginning at 5 p.m. PT/ 8 p.m. ET.
The ceremony will be held at Peacock Theater in Los Angeles.
How to Watch and Stream the 2026 Emmys
The show will be broadcast from coast-to-coast on NBC and will stream live and on demand on Peacock, as well.
Nights one and two from the Creative Arts Emmys will air on FXX on Saturday, Sept. 12, at 8 p.m. ET/PT. It will be available to stream on Hulu the following day.
Who Is Hosting the 2026 Emmys?
The Television Academy announced in July that Mariska Hargitay will emcee the event.

Hargitay has already won two Emmys for her film “My Mom Jayne,” taking home outstanding documentary and outstanding directing for a documentary/nonfiction program. The accolades make her a three-time Emmy winner.
Speaking about the honor during an appearance on TODAY in August, Hargitay shared that it took her a minute to process that she was being asked to host the major award show.
“I thought about it over the weekend and then I started going, ‘Why not?’” she recalled.

“Which is where I kind of am in my life,” the “Law & Order: SVU” star continued. “I was so incredibly honored and, again, knowing that it’s the first woman in 15 years was absolutely thrilling. And I am somebody to take on new challenges.”
Who Is Presenting at the 2026 Emmys?
Leading up to the ceremony, the Television Academy has been sharing groups of celebrities who will be presenters.
